RAG in Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling

Michael Glass, Gaetano Rossiello, Md Faisal Mahbub Chowdhury, Alﬁo Gliozzo · 2021

RAG is a model for slot filling. It first uses DPR to retrieve five relevant evidence passages, concatenates each passage with the query, and uses a BART-initialized sequence-to-sequence generator to predict the tail entity or answer. It marginalizes weighted next-token distributions across passages and trains the query encoder through their contribution to the correct output. In the KILT baseline, the Natural Questions-trained passage encoder remains fixed while the query encoder and generation component are fine-tuned. RAG produces the best slot fillers among tested baselines, though its retrieval is worse than BM25. Training on 500k T-REx instances takes two days on one NVIDIA P100 GPU.

Narrative, section by section

3 sections; each heading opens the text

Related Work .. DPR for Slot Filling

RAG first uses DPR to gather evidence passages and then uses a BART-initialized sequence-to-sequence model to generate an answer from each passage concatenated with the query. In the KILT baseline, only the query encoder and generation component are fine-tuned, while the passage encoder trained on Natural Questions remains fixed. RAG performs best among the tested baselines for producing slot fillers, but its retrieval performance is worse than BM25.

opening .. Dense Negative Sampling

RAG retrieves the top five relevant passages, concatenates each passage with the query, and uses a generator to predict the tail entity. It marginalizes weighted next-token distributions across passages and trains the query encoder through the passages’ contribution to the correct output.

KILT Experiments .. Slot Filling Evaluation

RAG uses retrieved passages for sequence-to-sequence generation and has a default of five passages per query in these experiments. The study evaluates RAG with its default Wikipedia index, BM25 retrieval, and a Natural Questions-trained DPR retriever.

retrieval-augmented generation methods in Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge

Wenhao Yu · 2022

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a general learning framework in the open-book setting that fuses pre-trained language models with traditional information retrieval techniques. It predicts an output from a source input and a document reference set by maximizing the output likelihood. Its two major components are a document retriever, which selects relevant documents, and a text generator, which produces output conditioned on retrieved references rather than generating from scratch. RAG explicitly and plug-and-play acquires external knowledge, can seek texts, tables, and knowledge graphs, and has received increasing NLP-community attention. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on many knowledge-intensive NLP downstream tasks while offering easy knowledge acquisition, strong scalability, and low training cost compared with conventional pre-trained generation models. Existing work has mainly retrieved unstructured text, especially Wikipedia passages or other general-domain corpora, from a single-source homogeneous retrieval space. The work therefore moves toward retrieval across heterogeneous knowledge sources to improve knowledge coverage and answer generation.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation methods have received increasing attention from the NLP community and achieved state-of-the-art performance on many NLP downstream tasks. They offer easy knowledge acquisition, strong scalability, and low training cost, and are examined for retrieving knowledge across heterogeneous knowledge.

opening

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fuses pre-trained language models with traditional information retrieval techniques in the open-book setting. It has achieved state-of-the-art performance on many knowledge-intensive NLP tasks, and its knowledge is explicitly acquired through retrieval while generation is conditioned on retrieved references. The unit notes that existing RAG work has focused mainly on retrieving unstructured text from general-domain corpora and proposes studying retrieval across heterogeneous knowledge.

2

RAG aims to predict y given x and a document reference set Z by maximizing the likelihood of y. It uses a document retriever to select relevant documents and a text generator to produce the desired output, and it can seek knowledge from external information sources.

3 / 3.1 .. 3.3.3

Retrieval-augmented generation is described as often relying on a single-source homogeneous retrieval space, especially Wikipedia passages. The unit proposes grounding it across heterogeneous knowledge sources to improve knowledge coverage and answer generation.

retrieval augmented LMs in Active Retrieval Augmented Generation

Zhengbao Jiang · 2023

Retrieval augmented LMs retrieve external information or documents from a user’s input to support generation, commonly using a retrieve-and-generate setup. This single retrieval can outperform generative language models on short-form knowledge-intensive tasks with clear needs, but becomes limiting for complex long-form generation, which may require additional retrieval during generation.

Narrative, section by section

2 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval augmented LMs retrieve information from external knowledge resources to support generation. Most existing retrieval augmented LMs use a retrieve-and-generate setup that retrieves information only once based on the input, which limits them in longer generation scenarios.

Introduction

Retrieval augmented language models commonly retrieve documents from a user's input and generate an answer conditioned on those documents. Single-time retrieval is effective for short-form knowledge-intensive tasks when the information needs are clear in the input, but complex long-form generation may require additional retrieval during generation.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy

Zhihong Shao, Yeyun Gong, Yelong Shen, Minlie Huang, Nan Duan, Weizhu Chen · 2023

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a promising approach to outdated knowledge and hallucinations in large language models. It retrieves knowledge, initially with the task input as query, prepends it to question q, and uses Chain-of-Thought prompting to produce a response based on retrieved knowledge. Retrieval can supply relevant facts but also differing information, as in the Jesse Hogan example. ITER-RETGEN extends the process: each output becomes context for retrieving additional knowledge in later iterations, rather than directly incorporating previous generations for refinement, and could be a strong research baseline.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as a promising approach for addressing outdated knowledge and hallucinations in large language models. The paper improves it through the iterative retrieval-and-generation method ITER-RETGEN.

1

Retrieval-augmented generation produces a response to a task input based on all retrieved knowledge, initially retrieved using the task input as the query. Within ITER-RETGEN, its output provides context for retrieving additional knowledge.

2

Retrieval-Augmented Generation supplies generated responses with retrieved knowledge. In the example concerning the 2015 AFL Rising Star award, retrieval identifies Jesse Hogan as the winner and provides differing height information, while iterative retrieval and generation are presented as a way to improve the answer.

3 / 3.1 .. 3.4

Retrieval-Augmented Generation produces an output using Chain-of-Thought prompting while prepending retrieved knowledge to the question q. Previous generations are not incorporated directly for refinement in this setup.

6

ITER-RETGEN could serve as a strong baseline for future research on retrieval-augmented generation.

RAG in Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding

Wenyu Huang, Mirella Lapata, Pavlos Vougiouklis, Nikos Papasarantopoulos, Jeff Z. Pan · 2023

RAG is a retrieve-generate architecture and encoder-decoder backbone. It first retrieves question-relevant passages from external knowledge sources, then generates responses from them; at inference it uses the top-5 retrieved passages. Its retriever and generator are jointly trained under label-answer supervision, and retrieval is marginalized. RAG tends to capture label-relevant, high-token-matching passages, retrieving Passage 1 but failing to retrieve Passage 2 because of label relevance. It is compared with DPR, marginally outperforming non-finetuned DPR by 1.9% Recall@1. Used as a baseline and main comparison model, it achieves reported retrieval and generation scores on MSMARCO and KILT-WoW, but performs worse than the proposed methods, generalizes badly in robustness evaluation, and can hallucinate answers.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

RAG uses a retrieve-generate architecture: it first retrieves question-relevant passages and then generates responses based on them. In the example, RAG favors the label-relevant passage and fails to retrieve another knowledge-relevant passage.

Related Works

RAG marginalizes the retrieval step and jointly trains the generator and retriever under supervision from the label answer. It outperforms DPR and serves as a retrieve-generate backbone in the proposed architecture.

Methodology / Retrieve-Generate Backbone .. Overall Architecture

RAG provides the retrieve-generate architecture chosen as the backbone for applying the knowledge-constrained objectives.

Experimental Setup / Datasets .. Comparison Models

It is the encoder-decoder backbone of the proposed methods and serves as the main comparison model. The experiments train an RAG model with the same configuration as the proposed methods; it obtains 10.7 R@1 and 58.6 ROUGE-L on MSMARCO, and 42.21 R-Precision and 15.68 ROUGE-L on KILT-WoW.

Results / RQ1: Effectiveness / Generative QA .. Case Studies

RAG serves as the baseline model. It performs worse than the proposed methods on retrieval and generation, generalizes badly in the robustness evaluation, and produces a hallucinated answer claiming that Gouda cheese is made from goat’s milk.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding

Wenyu Huang, Mirella Lapata, Pavlos Vougiouklis, Nikos Papasarantopoulos, Jeff Z. Pan · 2023

Retrieval Augmented Generation is a modeling approach and Transformer-based retrieve-generate system for knowledge-intensive generation tasks. It retrieves external passages to support answer generation and addresses hallucination. Its backbone scores passages with a Dense Passage Retriever, selects top-n using Maximum Inner Product Search, and marginalizes token-generation probabilities to maximize a label sentence. State-of-the-art marginalized-output models may overfocus on label-relevant rather than question-relevant passages and answers; related methods add reranking, hindsight retrieval, or knowledge graphs.

Narrative, section by section

3 sections; each heading opens the text

Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding / Abstract

Retrieval Augmented Generation models retrieve passages from external knowledge sources to support answer generation. State-of-the-art models with marginalized output are described as focusing too much on label-relevant passages rather than question-relevant passages and answers.

Related Works

Retrieval augmented generation uses retrieve-generate architectures to address hallucination in generated responses. Methods discussed in this unit improve generation by incorporating retrieved passages, reranking, hindsight retrieval, or knowledge graphs.

Methodology / Retrieve-Generate Backbone .. Overall Architecture

The retrieve-generate backbone uses a Dense Passage Retriever to score passages, selects the top-n passages with Maximum Inner Product Search, and marginalizes their token-generation probabilities. Its generation objective maximizes the probability of the label sentence.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Semantic Embeddings for Arabic Retrieval Augmented Generation

Hazem Abdelazim · 2023

Retrieval Augmented Generation is an AI framework and two-phase pipeline, introduced by Facebook Researchers in 2020, that combines information retrieval with generation of contextually relevant responses. First, its retrieval module finds pertinent text chunks from external sources or a corpus; then Large Language Models use that context for comprehension and response. Its critical information-retrieval component gives generative AI access to external knowledge and improves factual grounding, contextual relevance, accuracy, capabilities, scalability, adaptability, and customizability. The study explores semantic embedding and Retrieval Augmented Generation in the Arabic language, examining embedding size, tokenizer algorithms, re-ranking strategies, cross-encoder architectures, and language-sensitive evaluation, while proposing research to improve efficiency and applicability across linguistic contexts.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract—In recent times, Retrieval Augmented Generation

Retrieval Augmented Generation models have attracted considerable attention because of the impressive capabilities of Large Language Models. The study examines semantic embedding as a core component of the information retrieval process within Retrieval Augmented Generation systems.

I.

Retrieval Augmented Generation, introduced by Facebook Researchers in 2020, combines retrieval of pertinent information from external sources with generation of contextually relevant responses. It improves the factual grounding, contextual relevance, scalability, adaptability, and customizability of generative AI systems.

II. / A. Phase I: Information retrieval .. B. Phase 2: LLM Comprehension and Response

Retrieval Augmented Generation uses a two-phase pipeline consisting of information retrieval followed by LLM comprehension and response. It retrieves relevant text chunks from a corpus and supplies them as context to a large language model.

VI.

Retrieval Augmented Generation models are explored in the context of the Arabic language, with particular attention to their Information Retrieval component.

VII.

Retrieval Augmented Generation systems are examined in relation to embedding size, tokenizer algorithms, re-ranking strategies, cross-encoder architectures, and language-sensitive evaluation. Future research is proposed to improve their applicability and efficiency across diverse linguistic contexts.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in SELF-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

Akari Asai, Zeqiu Wu, Yizhong Wang, Avirup Sil, Hannaneh Hajishirzi · 2023-10-17

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is an ad hoc generation method for augmenting language-model inputs with retrieved text passages or external information. It retrieves relevant knowledge to support generation, improves knowledge-intensive tasks after fine-tuning or with off-the-shelf language models, and can decrease factual inaccuracies and errors. Common approaches retrieve a fixed number of passages, often once at the beginning, then prepend top retrieved documents to a query before models such as Llama2 or Alpaca generate an output. Its central limitation is indiscriminate retrieval: passages may be unnecessary, off-topic, or irrelevant even when factual grounding is not helpful, reducing versatility and producing unhelpful responses. Even relevant passages do not guarantee consistent generation or that outputs follow them. Adaptive retrieval approaches extend this pattern but have reduced runtime efficiency, robustness to irrelevant context, and attributions. In contrast, SELF-RAG evaluates whether sources are relevant and support the generated output.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

ABSTRACT

Retrieval-Augmented Generation augments language models by retrieving relevant knowledge and decreases factual inaccuracies. However, indiscriminately retrieving a fixed number of passages, regardless of whether retrieval is necessary or the passages are relevant, can diminish versatility or lead to unhelpful responses.

INTRODUCTION

Retrieval-Augmented Generation augments LLM inputs with relevant retrieved passages and can reduce factual errors in knowledge-intensive tasks. It may retrieve unnecessary or off-topic passages, reduce versatility, and does not guarantee that outputs follow relevant passages.

RELATED WORK

Retrieval-Augmented Generation augments language-model input with retrieved text passages and has improved knowledge-intensive tasks after fine-tuning or when used with off-the-shelf language models. Prior approaches often retrieve once at the beginning, while newer approaches adapt retrieval, jointly train retrievers and language models, or use retrieved passages during instruction tuning.

SELF-RAG: LEARNING TO RETRIEVE, GENERATE AND CRITIQUE / 3.1 / PROBLEM FORMALIZATION AND OVERVIEW .. 3.3 / SELF-RAG INFERENCE

Retrieval-augmented generation is contrasted with SELF-RAG because common approaches retrieve passages indiscriminately, whereas SELF-RAG evaluates whether retrieved sources are relevant and support the generated output.

EXPERIMENTS / 4.1 / TASKS AND DATASETS .. 4.3 / EXPERIMENTAL SETTINGS

Standard RAG baselines generate outputs with Llama2 or Alpaca after the query is prepended with top retrieved documents. They use the same retriever as SELF-RAG.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in How to Build an Adaptive AI Tutor for Any Course Using Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG)

Chenxi Dong · 2023-11-29

Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds Large Language Model responses in verified source materials to address information hallucination. It retrieves context by embedding queries and knowledge-base documents in a shared vector space and relying on semantic similarity. This partially addresses factual accuracy and coherent, context-aware instruction, but pure semantic similarity cannot capture structured conceptual relationships; it can retrieve isolated snippets, yielding incomplete, disconnected answers and limited effectiveness in education. In the AI Tutor, standard RAG serves as the baseline against KG-RAG, which adds knowledge-graph traversal for interconnected context. Students using standard RAG formed the Control Group and had a mean assessment score of 4.71 out of 10.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract—Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) in

Retrieval-Augmented Generation partially addresses factual accuracy and instructional coherence challenges. Its reliance on pure semantic similarity limits its effectiveness in educational contexts where conceptual relationships are important.

I. INTRODUCTION

Retrieval-augmented generation relies on semantic similarity but cannot capture structured relationships between concepts. In the subprime-crisis example, standard RAG retrieves isolated text snippets that may produce incomplete and disconnected answers.

II. FOUNDATIONS OF KG-RAG

Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds Large Language Model responses in verified source materials to address information hallucination. It retrieves relevant context by embedding queries and knowledge-base documents into a shared vector space.

III. AI TUTOR DESIGN: THE KG-RAG SOLUTION

Retrieval-augmented generation is integrated with a knowledge graph in the AI Tutor implementation. Unlike traditional RAG, KG-RAG uses knowledge graph traversal to provide interconnected context rather than isolated text snippets.

IV. AI TUTOR EVALUATION

Retrieval-Augmented Generation provides baseline responses in the comparison with KG-RAG. In the controlled experiment, students using standard RAG formed the Control Group and achieved a mean assessment score of 4.71 out of 10.

Retrieval-augmented Text Generation in Lift Yourself Up: Retrieval-augmented Text Generation with Self-Memory

Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) · 2023-12-23

Retrieval-augmented Text Generation is a generation paradigm that equips a small fine-tuned model or an LLM with an external database or memory bank containing knowledge or demonstration examples. It retrieves memory from a datastore, often the training corpus or training set, using the source, then generates a target conditioned on the source-memory pair. It matters because external retrieval can enhance generation quality and supports tasks including machine translation, dialogue response generation, summarization, code generation, language modeling, question answering, and semantic parsing. The described work addresses it through Selfmem, which enhances a generation model with its own output and is reported to improve generation quality over other retrieval-augmented generation models.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented text generation equips a small fine-tuned model or an LLM with access to an external database, typically the training corpus, and generates text using both the input and retrieved memory. It is studied in neural machine translation, dialogue response generation, and language modeling.

Related Work / Retrieval-augmented Text Generation .. Neural Text Reranking

It equips models with external memory containing additional knowledge or useful demonstration examples. It has been applied to machine translation, dialogue response generation, summarization, code generation, paraphrase generation, language modeling, counterfactual data generation, open-domain question answering, and semantic parsing.

Methods / Generation as Memory .. Implementation Details

Retrieval-augmented generation first retrieves memory from a datastore using the source and then generates the target from the source-memory pair. The datastore in this work is the training set.

Conclusion

Retrieval-augmented text generation is addressed through the Selfmem framework, which enhances a generation model with its own output.

Limitations

The paper proposes a general idea for retrieval-augmented generation. Selfmem is compared with other retrieval-augmented generation models and achieves improved generation quality.

retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

Jon Saad-Falcon · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a prominent approach for user-facing NLP applications such as question answering, fact-checking, and customer support. It bolsters language models by combining them with retrieval systems that gather domain-specific knowledge, ground generations in factual information, and cite sources for transparency or interpretability. Experiments assess retrieval-plus-generation systems using selected KILT and SuperGLUE datasets, while ARES targets RAG evaluation and is reported to outperform RAGAS.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

Jon Saad-Falcon · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation systems typically combine a retriever and a downstream language model. Given a user question, the retriever finds relevant corpus passages and the language model uses them to generate a response. Their designs vary through choices including retrieval models, document chunking, prompting or fine-tuning, and constraints from domain, corpus size, cost, and latency. Traditionally, they have relied on hand annotations for queries, retrieved passages, and responses. ARES provides an automated evaluation framework that uses sampled in-domain query-document-answer triples to score context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance, then ranks systems by confidence-interval midpoints. It uses only a few hundred human annotations and accurately assesses systems across eight knowledge-intensive tasks and datasets. Experiments create mock systems with known positive and negative examples and nine splits spanning 70% to 90% success rates, 2.5 points apart, to test scoring and ranking. Domain applications may require annotators with specialized knowledge.

Narrative, section by section

8 sections; each heading opens the text

ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems are the systems for which ARES provides an automated evaluation framework.

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation systems have traditionally been evaluated using hand annotations for input queries, passages to retrieve, and responses to generate. ARES evaluates these systems across context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance, accurately assessing them across eight knowledge-intensive tasks while using only a few hundred human annotations.

Introduction

A RAG system typically consists of a retriever and a downstream language model (LM). Given a user question, its retriever finds relevant passages from a corpus and its language model uses those passages to generate a response. Its design involves choices such as the retrieval model, how documents are divided into retrieval chunks, and how the language model is prompted or fine-tuned to use the retrieved information.

opening

RAG systems are evaluated by ARES according to whether they retrieve relevant contexts and generate answers that are both faithful and relevant. The unit states that RAG design choices vary across data domains, corpus sizes, and cost or latency budgets.

ARES .. 3.3

RAG systems are evaluated using sampled in-domain query-document-answer triples. ARES scores their context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance, then ranks systems using the midpoints of their confidence intervals.

Experiments / 4.1 .. 4.3

The experiments construct mock RAG systems with known positive and negative query-passage and query-passage-answer examples. Nine dataset splits represent systems with success rates from 70% to 90%, separated by 2.5 percentage points, allowing ARES to be tested on scoring and ranking.

Conclusion

RAG systems are evaluated by ARES through separate context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance scores. Across eight datasets in KILT, SuperGLUE, and AIS, ARES accurately scores and ranks these systems.

Limitations

The RAG system’s domain application determines whether annotators need specialized knowledge to produce the annotations used by ARES.

retrieval-augmented generation in An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Kun Zhu, Xiaocheng Feng, Xiyuan Du, Yuxuan Gu, Weijiang Yu, Haotian Wang, Qianglong Chen, Zheng Chu, Jingchang Chen, Bing Qin · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation is a generation approach that combines large language models with relevant information retrieved from an extensive corpus during inference. It commonly concatenates retrieved passages with a query to improve output relevance, coherence, and factual accuracy. Its main practical difficulty is noisy real-world retrieval: weak retrievers and redundant or irrelevant passages can make correct answers incorrect. As retrieved evidence grows, it can also exceed context-window limits, raise computation, and reduce performance. The described work treats retrieval-augmented generation as the setting for information-bottleneck-based compression and noise filtering, aiming to retain information useful for grounded answers. Experiments supply generators with top-one or top-five DPR-retrieved passages and motivate filters that improve FFR while limiting TFR. The conclusion and limitations position the method as enhancing noise-filtering performance in retrieval-augmented generation.

Narrative, section by section

7 sections; each heading opens the text

An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Retrieval-Augmented Generation appears in the title as the setting in which the work considers effective noise filtering.

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation integrates large language models with relevant information retrieved from an extensive corpus, but it faces challenges with real-world noisy data. The proposed approach applies information bottleneck theory to improve noise filtration and answer generation.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation incorporates information from external knowledge sources during inference to improve relevance, coherence, and factual accuracy. Its effectiveness can be limited by weak retrieval and by redundant, noisy, or irrelevant retrieved content.

Noise Filtering .. Reinforcement Learning

Retrieval-augmented generation commonly concatenates retrieved passages with queries, but excessive or noisy evidence can exceed context limits, increase computation, and reduce performance. The unit applies compression and noise filtering to retain information useful for producing ground outputs.

Experiments / Experimental Settings / Datasets and Retrieval Corpus .. Length of Summary and Conciseness

Retrieval augmentation supplies the generator with top-one or top-five DPR-retrieved passages. Although it can provide useful information, noisy passages often cause correct answers to become incorrect, motivating filtering methods that improve FFR while limiting TFR.

Conclusion

It is the setting in which the information bottleneck principle is applied to noise filters.

Limitations

Retrieval-augmented generation is the setting in which the method enhances the performance of the noise filtering task.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in BERGEN: A Benchmarking Library for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

David Rau, Hervé Déjean, Nadezhda Chirkova, Thibault Formal, Shuai Wang, Stéphane Clinchant, Vassilina Nikoulina · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a knowledge-intensive NLP method and approach for addressing factuality challenges in Large Language Models by enhancing them with external knowledge. It retrieves relevant background documents or context segments from an external collection and explicitly provides them to a language model, enabling answers beyond the model’s internal knowledge. Formally, it consists of a ranking system R and a parametric generative language model θ, which use retrieved context c and user input x to produce response r; retrieval and reranking can provide top-5 passages to the LLM. Its central challenge is that results depend on a complex, multi-step pipeline: retrieval system, reranker, generator, dataset, collection, metric, and other design choices all matter. It therefore calls for unified, systematic training and evaluation. BERGEN standardizes experiments across retrieval, reranking, generation, training, and evaluation, supports varied architectures and resources, and emphasizes flexibility and extensibility through configuration files. Across hundreds of configurations, retrieval quality and dataset choice strongly shape outcomes. Improved retrieval, especially reranking, can substantially improve responses on suitable datasets such as KILT NQ, but retrieval may offer no benefit or reduce performance elsewhere; closed-book generation can outperform oracle retrieval on KILT ELI5 and KILT WoW. Evaluation uses retrieval performance, Match, and LLMEval across datasets, finding NQ suitable while ELI5 and WoW may be unsuitable for testing RAG. It is also evaluated on multilingual MKQA and XOR-TyDi QA, with improved multilingual performance across reported languages.

Narrative, section by section

12 sections; each heading opens the text

front matter

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the subject for which BERGEN is described as a benchmarking library.

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances Large Language Models with external knowledge. The unit studies best practices for systematically evaluating RAG approaches, focusing on question answering and comparing retrievers, rerankers, LLMs, metrics, and datasets.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation supplies a language model with relevant information retrieved from an external collection so that it can generate answers beyond its internal knowledge. Its performance depends on many pipeline configurations and design choices, including the retrieval system, reranker, language model, dataset, and evaluation metric.

Related Work

RAG research uses varied experimental configurations, including different datasets, collections, evaluation metrics, retrieval systems, and LLMs. The unit argues that RAG systems need a unified framework for systematic training and evaluation.

Task Definition

RAG consists of a ranking system R and a parametric generative language model θ. It uses retrieved context segments c and user input x to produce a response r.

Benchmarking Library BERGEN .. 4.7

Retrieval-Augmented Generation experiments are standardized by BERGEN across retrieval, reranking, generation, training, and evaluation stages. BERGEN supports experiments using multiple retriever architectures, LLMs, datasets, collections, and evaluation metrics.

Experiments .. 5.6

Retrieval-augmented generation performance depends strongly on retrieval quality and the dataset. Retrieval improves results for some datasets, but can reduce performance or provide no benefit for others.

6 .. Limitations

RAG systems are benchmarked by BERGEN through hundreds of experiments involving different pipeline configurations. The unit reports that improved retrieval, particularly through rerankers, can substantially improve their responses.

references

It is represented through foundational work on Retrieval-Augmented Generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks and later studies on evaluation, adaptive retrieval, summarized retrieval, long-context models, and dual instruction tuning.

B

RAG is evaluated using retrieval performance and the LLMEval metric across datasets. The analysis concludes that ELI5 and WoW may not be appropriate for testing RAG systems, while NQ appears suitable.

E

Retrieval-augmented generation is evaluated by providing retrieved passages to large language models and measuring Match and LLMeval performance. The unit reports RAG performance across multiple datasets and retrieval systems.

H

Retrieval-augmented generation is evaluated by comparing retrieval systems, reranking, generators, and oracle retrieval. Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine

Guangzhi Xiong, Qiao Jin, Zhiyong Lu, Aidong Zhang · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a widely adopted, promising solution to hallucinations and outdated knowledge in Large Language Models. It augments responses with relevant documents from up-to-date and trustworthy collections, grounding reasoning to improve transparency and support accurate, reliable answers to knowledge-intensive medical questions. Its flexible modules include document collections, retrievers, and backbone LLMs. For medical answer generation, it collects external knowledge; in the MEDRAG Toolkit, concatenated retrieved snippets are prepended to language-model input and generally outperform chain-of-thought without retrieval on the MIRAGE benchmark.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as a promising solution to hallucinations and outdated knowledge in large language models and has been widely adopted.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation provides Large Language Models with relevant documents from up-to-date and trustworthy collections. It can reduce the effects of hallucination and outdated knowledge while improving transparency by grounding reasoning in retrieved documents.

The MIRAGE Benchmark / Evaluation Settings .. Component Datasets

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is used because the medical questions are knowledge-intensive and because external information can support more accurate and reliable answer generation.

The MEDRAG Toolkit

Retrieval-augmented generation is evaluated for medical question answering through the MEDRAG Toolkit. The approach prepends concatenated retrieved snippets to the language model input and generally performs better than chain-of-thought without retrieval on the MIRAGE benchmark.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine

Guangzhi Xiong, Qiao Jin, Zhiyong Lu, Aidong Zhang · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a generation method for knowledge-intensive tasks. Proposed by Lewis et al. (2020), it integrates retrieved relevant information so large language models can be grounded in provided contexts, mitigating hallucinations and supplying up-to-date knowledge not encoded by the models. A RAG system has multiple flexible components, but best practices for choosing optimal settings for different medical purposes are lacking. Follow-up studies by Borgeaud et al., Ram et al., Gao et al., Jiang et al., and Mialon et al. improve on vanilla RAG.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs

Zheng Wang, Zhongyang Li, Zeren Jiang, Dandan Tu, Wei Shi · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a technique and retrieval-augmented generation method that selects relevant memories for a question and provides them as context to a large language model. It is used in EMG-RAG with an Editable Memory Graph for smartphone memories and personalized agents. It retrieves top-K memories, activates graph nodes, and uses an MDP to traverse the edited graph before generation. Its key concerns are context overhead, noise, and missed diverse memory combinations; it is evaluated through indexing, retrieval, and generation.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is combined with an Editable Memory Graph in EMG-RAG to use smartphone memories for personalized agents.

1

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is discussed as a way to retrieve relevant memories and provide them as context to a large language model. The unit notes that Needles in a Haystack can introduce context overhead and noise, while advanced approaches often use a fixed Top-K that may miss diverse memory combinations.

4 / 4.1 .. 4.4

RAG traverses the edited memory graph to select memories before passing them to a language model. The system first retrieves top-K memories, activates corresponding graph nodes, and then uses the MDP to guide traversal.

5 / 5.1 .. 5.2

RAG methods are evaluated through indexing, retrieval, and generation or related retrieval strategies, and are integrated with GPT-4, ChatGLM3-6B, and PanGu-38B. The comparison includes NiaH, Naive, M-RAG, Keqing, and EMG-RAG.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Information Needs of Large Language Models

Weihang Su, Yichen Tang, Qingyao Ai, Zhijing Wu, Yiqun Liu · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a retrieval-augmented strategy, solution, and framework that enhances large language models by retrieving relevant external knowledge from databases and incorporating it into model inputs. It is a prominent approach to mitigating hallucination and improving performance. Rather than relying only on traditional single-round retrieval from an initial input, it can support complex multi-step and long-form generation: output is truncated at a detected position, retrieved documents are added to a prompt, and generation resumes. Evaluations on 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, IIRC, and StrategyQA show improved performance over direct question answering, though poorly timed retrieval can be less helpful.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances large language models by retrieving relevant information from external databases and incorporating it into their inputs. Traditional methods generally use single-round retrieval based on the initial input and may be less effective for complex multi-step and long-form generation tasks.

2 / 2.1 .. 2.2

Retrieval-Augmented Generation strategies enhance large language models by incorporating retrieved external knowledge into the model input.

3 .. 3.3

Retrieval-augmented generation integrates external knowledge into continued language-model generation. In this unit, the output is truncated at the detected position, retrieved documents are added to a prompt, and generation resumes from the truncated output.

4 / 4.1 .. 4.5

The RAG framework is evaluated on 2WikiMultihopQA, HotpotQA, IIRC, and StrategyQA. The experiments assess its ability to perform multihop reasoning, reading comprehension, and commonsense reasoning.

5 / 5.1 .. 5.5

Single-round retrieval augmentation consistently improves LLM performance over direct question answering across the evaluated datasets. The results also show that retrieval augmentation can be less helpful when it is activated at an inappropriate position.

Zhenrui Yue, Huimin Zeng, Yimeng Lu, Lanyu Shang, Yang Zhang, and Dong Wang · 2024

Retrieval augmented generation is a text generation method that incorporates retrieved, selected external documents as evidence, enabling up-to-date knowledge without expensive retraining. It primarily addresses knowledge-intensive NLP tasks and aims to improve factuality and reduce hallucination. For online misinformation response generation, it remains under-researched; the described work explores evidence-based counter-responses by collecting scientific evidence and performing RLHF alignment.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Improving Assessment of Tutoring Practices using Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Zifei (FeiFei) Han · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a RAG-based prompt strategy and prompt-based evaluation approach that integrates external knowledge sources into prompting. For tutoring practice evaluation, it uses word embeddings to bring tutoring transcripts and tutoring principles into a GPT model, allowing prepared embeddings to supply relevant information, including social-emotional learning principles, for scores and evidence. Its Retriever identifies correct and incorrect uses of a practice and returns tutor dialogue as evidence; its Generator produces a final 0-to-5 score, with one point for each criterion met. Across GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, the strategy consistently produces the desired output. It yields correct, contextually relevant, precise evaluations of tutoring transcripts without hallucinations, with accuracy assessed through hallucination levels and correctness in generated assessment texts. It demonstrates more accurate performance and lower financial costs than the other evaluated prompting strategies, and is identified as the most cost-effective strategy for GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 Turbo. It is proposed for broader tutor assessment applications, including a wider range of real-world tutoring transcripts and assessment of building content skills and promoting inclusion.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering

Qingfei Zhao, Ruobing Wang, Yukuo Cen, Daren Zha, Shicheng Tan, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technology and generation approach that improves LLM response quality by retrieving external knowledge, including Wikipedia, before generation. It provides external factual evidence to mitigate “lost in the middle” and helps alleviate outdated and long-tail knowledge, hallucinations, and lack of domain expertise. Rather than directly processing entire long documents, it uses fixed-length chunks to keep input concise and relevant. However, chunking can disrupt global long-context information, while direct use of retrieved chunks and low-quality retrieval can yield incomplete information and substantial noise. In evaluations, RAG includes Vanilla RAG and advanced baselines; LongRAG variants generally improve on HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, and MusiQue. LongRAG’s extraction and filtering are reported to provide higher-quality, less noisy knowledge and to outperform advanced and Vanilla RAG methods.

RAG systems are evaluated using retrieval and generation components, with LongRAG compared against advanced RAG and vanilla RAG approaches. The experiments find that LongRAG's extraction and filtering provide higher-quality, less noisy knowledge than standard approaches.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in M-RAG: Reinforcing Large Language Model Performance through Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Multiple Partitions

Zheng Wang, Shu Xian Teo, Jieer Ouyang, Yongjun Xu, Wei Shi · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a paradigm and framework within Large Language Models that retrieves relevant memories or information from an external database before answering questions or generating text, grounding generation in what is retrieved. It matters because whole-database retrieval can lose focus on crucial memories and introduce noise, while RAG also faces low precision, hallucination, redundancy, and context-window limitations. The work reviews Naive, Advanced, and Modular RAG, then proposes M-RAG: independent retrieval over multiple database partitions for finer-grained retrieval. M-RAG has inference complexity comparable to naive RAG, and experiments comparing Naive RAG, Self-RAG, Selfmem, and M-RAG find that adding RAG generally improves performance over no RAG. The conclusion emphasizes multiple partitions to improve retrieval and overall performance, while noting execution challenges across partitions.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances Large Language Models by retrieving relevant memories from an external database. Existing methods typically organize all memories in a whole database, which can limit focus on crucial memories and introduce noise.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant information from an external database before an LLM answers a question or generates text. The unit proposes performing RAG across multiple database partitions to support fine-grained retrieval and improve generation.

Related Work

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is reviewed through the categories of Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, and Modular RAG. The unit states that RAG can face low precision, hallucination, redundancy, and context-window limitations, and describes methods intended to address these issues.

Methodology .. 3.4 / The M-RAG Framework

Retrieval-augmented generation is implemented in M-RAG through independent retrieval processes over multiple database partitions. M-RAG has inference complexity comparable to naive retrieval-augmented generation, although its partitioned retrieval performs searches across partitions.

Experiments / Experimental Setup .. Experimental Results

Retrieval-augmented generation methods are compared through Naive RAG, Self-RAG, Selfmem, and M-RAG. The experiments show that adding RAG generally improves language-model performance over using no RAG.

Conclusion and Limitations

RAG is addressed through a multiple partition approach intended to improve retrieval and overall system performance. The paper focuses on challenges involved in executing RAG across multiple partitions.

Yiyun Zhao, Hanoz Bhathena, Prateek Singh, Saket Sharma, Bernardo Ramos, Aviral Joshi, Swaroop Gadiyaram · 2024

Retrieval Augmented Generation is a prominent approach for grounding LLM generations in up-to-date, domain-specific knowledge. It connects LLMs to live or updated sources by retrieving relevant documents and supplying them with the query, conversation history, and generation instructions. It can reduce hallucinations and improve answer quality without costly, brittle domain-specific fine-tuning. Its components are systematically investigated for real-world generation quality and optimized in the financial domain.

RAG systems in Optimizing LLM Based Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipelines in the Financial Domain

Yiyun Zhao, Hanoz Bhathena, Prateek Singh, Saket Sharma, Bernardo Ramos, Aviral Joshi, Swaroop Gadiyaram · 2024

RAG systems combine retrieval and generation: a retriever fetches documents likely relevant to a user query, then the documents, query, conversation history, and instructions enter an LLM context for answer generation. Their outputs are studied across six LLMs and two banking-sector datasets, evaluating answer quality, instruction following, retriever quality, document order and quantity, models, and prompts. Retrieval quality is central: when relevant context is missing or retrieval fails, systems may show pseudo-helpfulness, produce related but nonresponsive answers, and hallucinate. The analysis yields design recommendations for retrieval pipelines, prompts, and generation models.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

RAG systems are the subject of design recommendations formulated from the study's analysis of retrieval pipelines, prompts, and generation models.

1

A RAG system uses a retriever to fetch documents likely to be relevant to a user query and feeds them into the LLM's context for answer generation. This unit evaluates the effects of retriever quality, document order and quantity, generative models, and prompts on the system's output.

2 / 2.1 .. Evaluation Metrics and Aspects

RAG systems are evaluated with respect to answer quality and instruction following ability, with particular attention to the effects of retrieval quality on answer generation.

3 / 3.1 .. 3.4

LLM-based RAG systems can exhibit pseudo-helpfulness by attempting to answer when relevant information is missing from the context. This can produce related but nonresponsive content and hallucinations.

RAG in PlanRAG: A Plan-then-Retrieval Augmented Generation for Generative Large Language Models as Decision Makers

Myeonghwa Lee, Seonho An, Min-Soo Kim · 2024

RAG is a high-level technique and approach that augments language-model generation with external data. A retriever first finds data related to an input, such as a question, including results from database D through data-analysis queries; a language model then generates a response from the retrieved observations. Existing RAG-based methods mainly address knowledge-based question answering and make a decision through a single type of reasoning. In single-turn RAG, retrieval happens once; in iterative RAG, retrieval and generation occur multiple times. RAG can mitigate hallucination and biased answers to some extent, but these issues can still occur. In the reported experiments, it was not powerful enough to solve the decision-making task well, motivating high-level techniques for Decision QA rather than low-level RAG methods.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is described as a technique in which a retriever finds external data relevant to a question and provides it to a language model for answer generation. The unit notes that existing RAG-based methods mainly address knowledge-based question answering.

Methodology: PlanRAG

Existing RAG answers the best decision by reasoning over results retrieved from database D through data analysis queries. It is called single-turn RAG when retrieval occurs once and iterative RAG when retrieval occurs multiple times.

Related Work

RAG augments language-model generation with external data by retrieving information related to an input and generating a response from the retrieved observations. Most RAG methods are single-turn, while later methods perform retrieval and generation iteratively; the unit reports that RAG was not powerful enough to solve the decision-making task well in the experiments.

Limitations

The authors propose techniques from a high-level RAG technique perspective for solving Decision QA. Low-level RAG methods are not the focus of the paper.

Ethical Considerations

RAG methods mitigate hallucination and bias issues to some extent. Their use does not imply that these issues no longer occur.

retrieval augmented generation (RAG) in R2AG: Incorporating Retrieval Information into Retrieval Augmented Generation

Fuda Ye, Shuangyin Li, Yongqi Zhang, Lei Chen · 2024

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) is a framework and method that augments large language models with external documents provided by retrievers. It retrieves documents useful to a query, binds them with the query through a predefined prompt template, and has an LLM generate an answer. RAG integrates external, non-parametric knowledge and gives LLMs flexible access to vast, up-to-date data, improving performance in domain-specific and knowledge-intensive tasks and extending to audio, images, and knowledge graphs through modality-specific retrievers. Its central limitations are sensitivity to retrieval results, increased complexity, and a semantic gap or miscommunication between retrievers and LLMs, especially when documents are noisy, numerous, or long. The unit introduces R2AG as an enhanced framework intended for this retrieval-and-generation setting.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

front matter .. Abstract

Retrieval augmented generation applies large language models to scenarios in which external documents are provided by retrievers. The unit presents R2AG as an enhanced framework for this approach.

Introduction

RAG integrates external, non-parametric knowledge from retrievers into LLM generation. It has shown benefits in domain-specific and knowledge-intensive tasks, but its reliance on simple text concatenation creates difficulties in handling noisy, numerous, or overly long retrieved documents.

Related Works / Retrieval Augmented Generation .. Enhanced RAG

Retrieval Augmented Generation combines a retrieval component with large language models by binding retrieved documents with the original query and placing them in the model inputs. It gives large language models flexible access to vast, up-to-date data, but remains sensitive to retrieval results and has increased complexity.

R2AG / Problem Formulation and Overview .. Training Strategy

RAG prompts an LLM to generate answers from a query and documents returned by a retriever. Its standard prompt-based pipeline can create miscommunication and a semantic gap between the retriever and the LLM.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment

Kelong Mao, Zheng Liu, Hongjin Qian, Fengran Mo, Chenlong Deng, Zhicheng Dou · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a paradigm for enhancing text generation and applying large language models by integrating external knowledge through a standing-by retriever. It matters because authoritative, up-to-date information can improve generated outputs’ truthfulness and credibility, although off-the-shelf systems can underperform in specialized domains. The work moves from this motivation to domain adaptation through fine-tuning retrievers and generators in a unified system, then evaluates retrieval versus no retrieval. Retrieval substantially improves domain-specific question answering, while fine-tuning without retrieval can reduce GPT-4 accuracy.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is presented as an effective paradigm that improves text generation by integrating large language models with external knowledge. The abstract focuses on adapting general RAG systems to specialized domains.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is described as a popular paradigm for applying large language models by integrating a retrieval component. It can improve the truthfulness and credibility of generated outputs by providing authoritative and up-to-date information, but off-the-shelf systems often underperform in specialized domains.

Related Work / RAG Fine-tuning .. Self-Alignment

Retrieval-augmented generation systems have been enhanced through fine-tuning of their retrievers and generators. The described work targets a unified system that includes both components.

Experiments / Setup / Datasets and evaluation metrics .. and Retriever Combinations

Retrieval-augmented generation is evaluated by comparing systems with and without retrieval. The results show that retrieval substantially improves domain-specific question answering and that fine-tuning without retrieval can reduce GPT-4 accuracy.

retrieval-augmented generation in RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment

Kelong Mao, Zheng Liu, Hongjin Qian, Fengran Mo, Chenlong Deng, Zhicheng Dou · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation is a question-answering system with a retriever and generator, including large language models. It retrieves relevant information from an external knowledge database, then generates an answer using that information. RAG-Studio adapts RAG systems to domains by jointly fine-tuning both components with synthetic domain-specific training data.

Narrative, section by section

3 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

RAG-Studio jointly fine-tunes the RAG system using synthetic domain-specific training data. This process enables the retriever to provide more precise information and the LLM to use retrieved information more effectively.

Methodology / Preliminaries .. Fine-tuning RAG Models

Retrieval-augmented generation first retrieves relevant information from an external knowledge database and then generates an answer by incorporating the retrieved information. In this unit, it is adapted to domain-specific applications through fine-tuning.

Conclusion

RAG systems are the target of RAG-Studio's domain adaptation framework. The framework enables efficient fine-tuning of their retriever and generator components.

RAG systems in RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation

Shahul Es, Jithin James, Luis Espinosa-Anke, Steven Schockaert · 2024

RAG systems are retrieval augmented generation systems composed of a retrieval module and an LLM-based generation module. They supply large language models with knowledge from a reference corpus, helping keep them up to date and reduce hallucination risk. Their behavior depends on the retrieval model, corpus, language model, and prompt formulation, and implementation requires significant tuning. They are evaluated with perplexity or question answering, despite limitations, and are the subject of an automated reference-free evaluation framework; accurate, fair systems are encouraged.

RAG systems are composed of a retrieval module and an LLM-based generation module. They provide large language models with knowledge from a reference corpus, which can help keep systems up to date and reduce the risk of hallucinations.

opening

A RAG system is affected by its retrieval model, corpus, language model, and prompt formulation. It can be evaluated through measures such as perplexity or question answering, although these approaches have limitations.

7

RAG systems are the subject of the proposed automated reference-free evaluation framework.

opening

The text discusses the implications of enabling large user bases to use more accurate RAG systems. It states that fair systems should continue to be encouraged on top of RAGAS.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation

Shahul Es, Jithin James, Luis Espinosa-Anke, Steven Schockaert · 2024

Retrieval Augmented Generation is a standard retrieval-augmented generation system that addresses language-model limitations, including post-training-event and rare-knowledge issues. Given a question, it retrieves relevant passages or context from a corpus and feeds them with the question to a language model, which generates an answer. Performance depends on retrieval, corpus, language model, and prompt formulation; evaluation uses reference-free metrics and can be end-to-end.

opening

Retrieval Augmented Generation addresses limitations of language models by retrieving relevant passages from a corpus and providing them, together with the original question, to the language model. Its performance depends on factors including the retrieval model, corpus, language model, and prompt formulation.

3 .. Faithfulness

RAG systems retrieve context for a question and use that context to generate an answer. They are evaluated using reference-free metrics because human-annotated datasets or reference answers are usually unavailable.

8

The toolkit is aimed at providing an end-to-end evaluation framework for RAG.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework in RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Kiseung Kim and Jay-Yoon Lee · 2024

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a framework and traditional QA system that combines parametric knowledge with external, nonparametric knowledge for open-domain question answering and knowledge-intensive natural language generation. It uses a retriever to obtain query-related contexts and a generator to produce answers for question-context pairs, then aggregates or marginalizes answers across multiple contexts using document relevance or retrieval-based similarity scores. RAG has shown promising progress and state-of-the-art performance, and is easily adaptable to modern large language model. Its central limitation is performance degradation when irrelevant contexts accompany a query. More accurate question-context relevance measurement, including a relevance estimator, improves open-domain QA performance and interpretability; RE-RAG outperforms traditional RAG with the same total parameters. High-confidence retrieved context enables efficient use by small models, while alternative knowledge sources help in low-confidence cases. Further modules remain a direction for exploration.

RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Retrieval-augmented generation is identified in the title as the setting in which a relevance estimator is used to improve open-domain QA performance and interpretability.

Abstract

The Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework combines parametric knowledge with external knowledge for open-domain question answering. Its performance degrades when a question is accompanied by irrelevant contexts.

Introduction

Retrieval augmented generation has shown promising progress in natural language generation, specifically for knowledge-intensive tasks. Traditional RAG aggregates answers from multiple contexts, weighting them by document relevance scores.

opening

Retrieval-augmented generation enhances faithfulness and reliability by combining nonparametric knowledge with parametric knowledge. Its accuracy can decline when the language model receives contexts that are not relevant to the query.

2 / 2.1 .. 2.3

Traditional RAG uses a retriever to obtain related contexts and a generator to produce answers from each question-context pair. It marginalizes answer probabilities across contexts using retrieval-based similarity scores.

3.4 / 4 / 4.1 .. 4.2

Traditional RAG is used as the comparison system for RE-RAG. RE-RAG performs better than traditional RAG despite having the same total number of parameters.

5 / 5.1 .. 5.3

Retrieval-augmented generation uses contextual knowledge retrieved for the query. The analysis finds that small models can use retrieval-augmented generation efficiently when the retrieved context has high confidence, while alternative knowledge sources are useful for low-confidence cases.

7

The authors hope their research inspires exploration of additional modules for retrieval-augmented generation.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Patrice Béchard · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is an approach that retrieves information from specific data sources before text generation to limit false or outdated information. Here it is adapted from factual retrieval to structured output, retrieving JSON objects that may form part of a generated document or workflow. Its central value is reducing hallucination while improving output quality, trustworthiness, and workflow generation, especially when correct output requires external knowledge. It reduces hallucinated steps to less than 7.5% and hallucinated tables to less than 4.5% with all StarCoderBase LLMs while maintaining overall performance. It also enables out-of-domain generalization without further fine-tuning and supports conservative generation when suggestions are absent. Finally, it can be deployed in limited-resource settings with a very small retriever and a small LLM without loss in performance.

RAG system in Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Patrice Béchard · 2024

The RAG system has a high-level architecture that initializes indices of steps and tables, then retrieves suggestions for each request, appends them to the query, and uses an LLM to generate JSON workflows. It trains a retriever encoder and LLM in a RAG fashion, supports domains including HR and finance, and is evaluated in- and out-of-domain.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Approach: Document Question Answering using Large Language Model

Kurnia Muludi, Kaira Milani Fitria, Joko Triloka, Sutedi · 2024

Retrieval Augmented Generation is a method for Question Answering systems and document processing in Natural Language Processing. It addresses document-processing and manual-reading limitations by combining vector-store search with text generation. Introduced by Patrick Lewis et al. in 2021, it combines parametric and non-parametric methods or memory: it retrieves relevant factual content from a knowledge base and external data sources, then uses that content as context for a Large Language Model to generate text. As a hybrid model and mechanism for retrieval and generation, it supports open-domain question answering, adapts to dynamic data, works flexibly with external knowledge sources, and aims to minimize or mitigate hallucinatory responses, including for QA tasks on internal organizational documents. In the proposed interactive document-question-answering system, submitted PDF documents are converted into embedded vector form. Retrieval-Augmented Generation is integrated with LangChain, FAISS, and GPT-3.5 or GPT-3.5-turbo to answer questions from documents. The study provides a proposed dataset for testing Question Answering document systems and contributes to benchmarking in research communities. Its findings highlight efficiency and competitiveness: it reports outperforming other QA applications on ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEU, and Jaccard Similarity, with 0.74 ROUGE precision, 0.88 BERTScore F1, 0.28 BLEU precision, and 0.33 Jaccard Similarity.

I.

Retrieval Augmented Generation is proposed for document question answering because it combines generative capabilities with retrieval from external knowledge sources. It can adapt to dynamic data, work with external data sources, and help mitigate hallucinatory responses.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation was introduced by Patrick Lewis et al. in 2021 as a method combining parametric and non-parametric approaches. It has demonstrated capabilities in open-domain question answering and is investigated in this study for document processing within an interactive question-answering system.

In this unit, it is used to construct the proposed document-based question-answering system and to reduce hallucinative responses.

IV. / A. Result .. G. Discussion

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is used to convert submitted PDF documents into embedded vector form and support question answering. The unit reports that combining LangChain and FAISS for RAG, together with GPT-3.5, provided good results.

RAG in Retrieval-augmented generation in multilingual settings

Association for Computational Linguistics · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a promising solution that augments user queries with relevant context retrieved from the Internet or a given collection, incorporating up-to-date or domain-specific knowledge into large language models and improving factuality, especially in knowledge-intensive tasks. Previously studied predominantly in English-only settings, it is examined in multilingual settings, including an application supporting 11 languages and 13 additional pretraining-only languages. RAG yields large improvements across languages on MKQA and XOR TyDi QA, while analysis investigates remaining English versus non-English gaps through prompting, generators, retrieval, and language ablations. The work also identifies query reformulation and context post-processing as standard practices and provides a baseline for future research.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as a promising solution for incorporating up-to-date or domain-specific knowledge into large language models and improving their factuality. The work extends its investigation beyond predominantly English-only settings.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has recently emerged as a promising solution for incorporating up-to-date or domain-specific knowledge into large language models. It augments user queries with relevant context retrieved from the Internet or a given collection.

opening

RAG is the application context in which the multilingual system is being considered. The application officially supports 11 languages and includes 13 additional languages in pretraining but not instruction tuning.

Results and discussion .. opening

RAG produces large performance improvements across languages on MKQA and XOR TyDi QA. Its remaining gap between English and non-English performance is examined through ablations of prompting, generators, retrieval, and language.

Conclusion

RAG is studied in multilingual settings. The work analyzes the impact of its components on overall performance and provides a baseline for future research.

Limitations

RAG is described as the context for common practice in evaluating open question answering with Wikipedia as the datastore.

retrieval-augmented generation in RetrievalQA: Assessing Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Short-form Open-Domain Question Answering

Zihan Zhang, Meng Fang, Ling Chen · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation augments large language models by retrieving relevant information, and has become popular for knowledge-intensive tasks such as open-domain question-answering. It generally improves QA performance when questions require knowledge absent from LLMs, though retrieved context can be noisy or irrelevant and distract models, reducing performance. In reported experiments, GPT-4 has the highest QA accuracy despite retrieving less often than some models.

opening

Retrieval-augmented generation is discussed through the limitations of adding retrieved context to model responses. Retrieved context can contain noise or irrelevant information and may distract large language models, reducing task performance.

RetrievalQA Challenges Adaptive RAG / 3.1 .. 3.4

RAG generally improves QA performance in the reported experiments because the questions require knowledge not present in the LLMs. GPT-4 achieves the highest QA accuracy despite retrieving less frequently than some other models.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Retrieving, Rethinking and Revising: The Chain-of-Verification Can Improve Retrieval Augmented Generation

Bolei He, Nuo Chen, Xinran He, Lingyong Yan, Zhenkai Wei, Jinchang Luo, and Zhen-Hua Ling · 2024

Retrieval Augmented Generation is an approach, framework, and method for addressing hallucinations in Large Language Models. It retrieves external contextual knowledge for an input question, then uses a language model to generate a response. Its system components include a retriever and a generator, and its WebGLM-based retrieval process includes coarse-grained web search and fine-grained LLM-augmented retrieval. By incorporating extensive, real-time knowledge from external sources, it expands knowledge boundaries and can enhance generation quality. However, it can face unsuitable original queries, incorrect retrieval, inconsistent generation with external references, repetitive answers, and internal generation errors. CoV-RAG addresses these weaknesses by training language model M with retrieved references, generated answers, and quality verification, and by integrating a verification module. Its inference process retrieves, rethinks, and revises; revising after initial retrieval and using multi-iteration retrieval improve results. CoV-RAG is presented as mitigating hallucinations in both external retrieval and internal generation stages.

Introduction

Retrieval augmented generation supplies externally retrieved knowledge to language models before they generate answers. It can mitigate hallucinations caused by limited model knowledge, but it remains vulnerable to retrieval errors and internal generation errors.

2 / Methods .. Algorithm 1 CoV-RAG Inference

Retrieval Augmented Generation retrieves external knowledge based on an input question and uses a language model to generate a response. The unit notes that generated answers may be inconsistent or repetitive and that retrieval may be incorrect when the question is unsuitable for effective retrieval.

2.3 / CoV-RAG Training

Retrieval-augmented generation is the task for which CoV-RAG trains language model M. The training includes retrieved references, generated answers, and verification of their quality.

4 / Results and Analysis / 4.1 / Main Results .. 4.4 / Further Analysis on Retriever

The unit evaluates retrieval-augmented generation methods using accuracy, GPT-4-based quality dimensions, ablations, and retrieval accuracy. It reports that revising after the initial retrieval and performing multi-iteration retrieval improve results.

5 / Related Work

Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as an approach for addressing hallucinations by using real-time retrieval results to expand the knowledge boundaries of large language models and enhance generation quality.

6 / Conclusion

Retrieval-augmented generation is addressed through CoV-RAG, which mitigates hallucinations in both internal generation and external retrieval stages.

RAG in Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Xiaohua Wang, Zhenghua Wang, Xuan Gao, Feiran Zhang, Yixin Wu, Zhibo Xu, Tianyuan Shi, Zhengyuan Wang, Shizheng Li, Qi Qian, Ruicheng Yin, Changze Lv, Xiaoqing Zheng, Xuanjing Huang · 2024

RAG is a retrieval-augmented generation technique and framework that combines pretraining models with retrieval-based models. Its central purpose is to enhance large language models by retrieving query-relevant documents from external knowledge bases, supplying accurate, real-time, domain-specific context. This can integrate up-to-date information, improve response quality and information accuracy, and mitigate or reduce hallucinations, particularly in specialized domains. It also supports rapid deployment for specific organizations and domains without updating model parameters when query-related documents are available. A typical RAG workflow has multiple processing steps: query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, and summarization. Fine-tuning optimizes retrievers and generators, while query-based summarization compresses retrieved material to address redundant information and lengthy prompts. The work examines existing RAG approaches, their combinations, and modular designs to search for optimal implementations. Its best practices include a Best Performance Practice and a Balanced Efficiency Practice, reflecting the tradeoff that frequent retrieval can increase response time. The study applies RAG to NLP, extends it to image generation through text2image and image2text retrieval, and identifies speech and video as future avenues. Code and resources are available at the FudanDNN-NLP/RAG repository.

Narrative, section by section

10 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

RAG techniques integrate up-to-date information, mitigate hallucinations, and enhance response quality, especially in specialized domains. The unit investigates existing RAG approaches and their combinations and proposes deployment strategies that balance performance and efficiency.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation combines the strengths of pretraining and retrieval-based models to enhance model performance and address outdated or fabricated information. It enables rapid deployment for specific organizations and domains without updating model parameters when query-related documents are available.

Related Work

Retrieval-augmented generation addresses hallucinations by retrieving relevant documents from external knowledge bases. It provides Large Language Models with accurate, real-time, domain-specific context.

Retriever and Generator Fine-tuning

RAG uses fine-tuning to optimize its retrievers and generators. The unit focuses on best practices for applying RAG methods and improving their use in LLMs.

RAG Workflow / Query Classification

Retrieval-augmented generation can improve information accuracy and reduce hallucinations, but frequent retrieval increases response time. It is used when knowledge beyond the model’s parameters is needed.

Summarization

Retrieval-augmented generation can provide redundant information and lengthy prompts, creating challenges for accurate responses and efficient inference. Query-based summarization methods are used to compress retrieved information within its pipeline.

Searching for Best RAG Practices

RAG is investigated to identify optimal implementation practices across its modules.

Discussion / Best Practices for Implementing RAG .. Multimodal Extension

RAG is implemented through modular practices involving query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, and summarization. It is extended to multimodal applications through text2image and image2text retrieval.

Conclusion

Retrieval-augmented generation is examined to identify practices that improve the quality and reliability of content produced by large language models. The study’s findings contribute to a deeper understanding of retrieval-augmented generation systems.

Limitations

The study discusses the application of RAG in NLP and extends its scope to image generation. It identifies speech and video as additional modalities for future exploration.

RAG system receives a query and contexts, using one corpus across tasks. It is evaluated with Faithfulness, Context Relevancy, Answer Relevancy, and Answer Correctness, including GPT scoring of ODQA and MultiHop QA.
