retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models in TRACE the Evidence: Constructing Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Jinyuan Fang · 2024

RAG models use a retriever-reader architecture, with retrieved documents supporting answer generation and large language models reading documents prepended to questions. They achieve remarkable QA performance but can degrade when irrelevant retrieval adds noise, especially in multi-hop reasoning. TRACE addresses this by constructing knowledge-grounded reasoning chains from retrieved documents.

Narrative, section by section

2 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

RAG models can suffer from noise introduced by irrelevant retrieved information, especially when answering multi-hop questions that require multiple reasoning steps.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models use a retriever-reader architecture in which retrieved documents support answer generation. Their performance can decline when irrelevant documents introduce noise, particularly for multi-hop questions. TRACE improves their multi-hop reasoning by constructing knowledge-grounded reasoning chains from retrieved documents.

retrieval-augmented generation in TRACE the Evidence: Constructing Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Jinyuan Fang · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation is a generation method and an effective approach for question answering and knowledge-intensive NLP tasks. It typically unfolds as a retriever-reader pipeline: a retriever obtains relevant information, then a reader generates answers from retrieved documents. It has shown strong QA performance and has been used for multi-hop questions and, in some applications, knowledge graph question answering. Its central limitation is retriever imperfection: irrelevant documents may be included and hinder answers. In the vanilla RAG baseline, all retrieved documents are given to the reader; TRACE-Triple and TRACE-Doc substantially improve on this baseline while often using less context.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in The Good and The Bad: Exploring Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Shenglai Zeng, Jiankun Zhang, Pengfei He, Yue Xing, Yiding Liu, Han Xu, Jie Ren, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin, Yi Chang, Jiliang Tang · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is an advanced natural language processing technique and system for enhancing large language model generation. It retrieves relevant knowledge from an external database or large document corpus, integrates retrieved documents with a user query, and then generates an answer. Its typical phases are retrieval and generation, and its core components are a dataset, retriever, and LLM; these can be exchanged or updated without retraining or fine-tuning the entire system. It boosts output accuracy and relevance, mitigates hallucinations, and is used in personal chatbots, medical chatbots, and medical diagnostic assistants. The records then emphasize a privacy tradeoff: incorporating retrieval data can reduce LLM memorization and leakage of training data, but can also expose sensitive retrieval data. In particular, it is susceptible to composite structured prompting attacks for extracting retrieval data. Thus, it reshapes LLM generation while introducing new, currently under-explored privacy issues.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation facilitates language models with proprietary and private data. The work finds that it can introduce privacy risks involving retrieval data while also mitigating leakage of large language models’ training data.

1 / Introduction

RAG enhances text generation by combining information retrieved from a large document corpus with an original query before generation by a large language model. The unit studies its privacy risks, finding that it can expose sensitive retrieval data while also reducing the tendency of LLMs to output memorized training data.

2 / Related Work / 2.1 / Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) .. 2.2 / Privacy Risk of Large Language Models

Lewis et al. (2020) introduced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) as an approach for enhancing large language model generation. It combines a dataset, retriever, and language model, whose components can be exchanged or updated without retraining or fine-tuning the entire system, and it is used in applications including personal chatbots and medical diagnostic assistants.

3 / Method / 3.1 / Background and Threat Model .. 3.3 / Privacy Leakage on LLM Training Data

Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines a large language model M, a retrieval dataset D, and a retriever R to produce an answer from a user query q and retrieved documents.

retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in The Good and The Bad: Exploring Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Shenglai Zeng, Jiankun Zhang, Pengfei He, Yue Xing, Yiding Liu, Han Xu, Jie Ren, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin, Yi Chang, Jiliang Tang · 2024

Retrieval-augmented generation is a technology that uses an external retrieval database during inference. It matters because it creates a privacy tradeoff: retrieval and generation can reproduce or closely resemble private database content, making the system vulnerable to attacks that extract private retrieval data. At the same time, integrating retrieval data can reduce reproduction of memorized training data, including targeted personal identifying information extraction and prefix-based text reconstruction. Empirical studies, attack methods, evaluation, mitigation discussion, and practical implications trace these risks and potential protections from setup through conclusions.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

RAG systems are shown through empirical studies and novel attack methods to be vulnerable to leaking a private retrieval database.

4 / RQ1: Can we extract private data from / 4.1 / Evaluation Setup .. 4.5 / Potential Mitigation

RAG is evaluated for its vulnerability to privacy attacks on external retrieval data. Its retrieval and generation components can reproduce or closely resemble private content from the retrieval database.

5 / RQ2: Can retrieval data affect the / 5.1 / Evaluation setup .. 5.4 / Discussions & Practical Implications

Retrieval-augmented generation is evaluated as a way to reduce the extraction of memorized information from models. Its use lowers both targeted personal identifying information extraction and successful prefix-based text reconstruction.

6 / Conclusions

The paper investigates the privacy risks of retrieval-augmented generation for LLMs. It suggests that RAG could potentially mitigate training data leakage by reducing LLMs’ tendency to output memorized training data.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Unified Active Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation

Qinyuan Cheng · 2024

Retrieval Augmented Generation is an approach to address LLM hallucination that retrieves relevant documents before generation and appends retrieved external information to the original user input through a RAG template. It aims to improve factual correctness, especially for questions requiring current or missing information, while directing the model to use only passages relevant to the question. Its central issue is that retrieval is not always beneficial: applying it to every instruction can add irrelevant or incorrect knowledge, increase latency, and impair creativity and versatility. Thus, always-retrieval uses it for every generation and never-retrieval for none, while UAR introduces selective retrieval to preserve internal capabilities and supply information when needed.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Unified Active Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation

This work concerns Retrieval Augmented Generation, as stated in its title.

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation does not always benefit from applying retrieval to every instruction, making retrieval decisions important for system performance.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation usually retrieves relevant documents before generating an answer to improve factual correctness. The unit explains that applying it to every instruction can impair creativity, introduce irrelevant knowledge, and increase latency, motivating more selective retrieval through UAR.

3 .. 3.3

Retrieval-augmented generation is supported by appending retrieved external information to the original user input using a RAG template. The prompt instructs the model to use only reference passages relevant to the question.

4 / 4.1 .. 4.7

Retrieval augmentation improves performance when questions require current or missing information but can interfere with the model when factual retrieval is unnecessary or external information is incorrect. UAR aims to invoke it selectively, preserving internal capabilities while supplying information for time-sensitive or unknown questions.

6

Retrieval-augmented generation is the area for which UAR is introduced as a unified active retrieval framework.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Association for Computational Linguistics · 2024

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a framework for modern NLP systems that enhances large language models by incorporating information retrieved from external databases or texts as context for generation. It supports text-generation applications including open-domain question answering and dialogue, is widely used in those areas and code generation, and aims to make generated text more accurate and credible. Its central challenge is that retrieval can yield fake, noisy, fragmented, incomplete, incorrect, or merely semantically related information, which may interfere with or mislead the language model. The records recast the role of LLMs in RAG as information refinement. In the described training setting, target generation is conditioned on constructed retrieved texts; the Correct and Complete task trains models to use noisy retrieved knowledge. INFO-RAG is presented as an unsupervised training method for improving use of retrieved information and robustness. Evaluation spans eleven datasets and seven tasks, including scenarios with correct answers, altered answers, or no correct answers in retrieved texts. The reported results show average improvement for all four LLaMA-2 variants, and the conclusion states advantages in ICL and robustness.

Narrative, section by section

10 sections; each heading opens the text

Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the application context identified in the work's title.

Abstract

RAG enhances large language models by incorporating additional information from retrieval. The unit presents INFO-RAG as a training method intended to improve model use of retrieved information in RAG and increase robustness.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation equips neural systems and large language models with retrieved information for generation tasks such as open-domain question answering and dialogue. The unit argues that RAG is challenged by fake, noisy, fragmented, incomplete, and incorrect retrieved information, and proposes improving it through information refinement.

Related Work / Retrieval Augmented Generation .. Our INFO-RAG

Retrieval Augmented Generation provides additional knowledge to language models by retrieving information from external databases. It is widely used in open-domain question answering, dialogue, and code generation, while noise in retrieved texts can interfere with or mislead the language model.

Positive Information Gain in RAG

RAG is the setting in which the role of LLMs is reassessed as information refinement. Its retrieval process may provide complete, incomplete, incorrect, or only semantically related texts for a question.

Unsupervised Learning .. Training Strategy

Retrieval-augmented generation is represented in the training tasks by conditioning target generation on constructed retrieved texts. The Correct and Complete task, in particular, trains the model to use noisy retrieved knowledge.

Experiments / Datasets and Evaluation Metrics .. Enhancing Previous SOTA in Open-Retrieval

The unit reports zero-shot retrieval-augmented generation results across eleven datasets and seven tasks. INFO-RAG improves the reported performance of all four LLaMA-2 model variants on average, with an average improvement of 9.39%.

Analysis / Fine-grained Analysis for Three Scenarios .. Avoid Catastrophic Forgetting Experiment on

The unit evaluates three retrieval-augmented generation scenarios according to whether retrieved texts contain correct answers, contain altered answers, or contain no correct answers.

Conclusion

RAG benefits from the proposed information refinement perspective and from INFO-RAG training. INFO-RAG improves LLM performance for RAG and shows advantages in ICL and robustness.

Limitations

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the setting in which the paper aims to enable large language models to perform information refinement.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Merging Mixture of Experts and Retrieval Augmented Generation for Enhanced Information Retrieval and Reasoning

Xingyu Xiong and Mingliang Zheng · 2024-02-23

Retrieval Augmented Generation is an advanced artificial-intelligence methodology, paradigm, and mechanism that extends a language model’s access to external information beyond its training dataset. It combines a document retrieval system with a generative model: during generation, a retrieval component searches external knowledge bases or databases for relevant documents, while the generative model incorporates those documents into its response. Documents and queries are projected into a high-dimensional vector space by an embedding function; dense vector searches and normalized similarity scores identify relevant material. The model then generates contextually relevant, factually enriched responses conditioned on retrieved information. Its central value is dynamic access to broad, up-to-date, and specialized knowledge, reported to improve accuracy, relevance, depth, complex question answering, domain-specific performance, reasoning, and task performance, while mitigating biases and inaccuracies. In the reported work, it is integrated into the Mistral 8x7B Large Language Model with Mixture of Experts and evaluated through accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and contextual quality. Implementation requires extracting relevant features and ensuring seamless retrieval and integration; alternative retrieval and integration mechanisms remain a future research direction.

Narrative, section by section

8 sections; each heading opens the text

front matter

Retrieval Augmented Generation is part of the article's title and is listed as a keyword for the research article.

Merging Mixture of Experts and Retrieval Augmented Generation for Enhanced Information Retrieval and Reasoning / Abstrac

Retrieval Augmented Generation is integrated into the Mistral 8x7B Large Language Model. The integration is evaluated for its ability to improve accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and the contextual quality of generated responses.

I. INTRODUCTION

Retrieval Augmented Generation uses external knowledge bases during generation to retrieve and incorporate relevant information in real time. It is combined with Mixture of Experts to address limitations in the information retrieval and reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models.

II. RELATED WORK / A. Limitations of LLMs in Information Retrieval and Reason- .. C. RAG

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates a retrieval component with a generative model so that external data can be incorporated dynamically into generation. Studies report improvements in factual accuracy, relevance, specialized-domain performance, complex question answering, and the mitigation of biases and inaccuracies in generated content.

III. METHODOLOGY / A. Model Architecture .. D. Dataset and Evaluation Metrics

Retrieval-Augmented Generation extends the model’s access to information beyond its training dataset by retrieving relevant documents from an external database. Document and query embeddings are compared to produce retrieval scores, and the generative model uses the retrieved documents to produce factually enriched responses.

IV. RESULTS / A. Implementation .. C. Qualitative Analysis

RAG was integrated into the Mistral model to support information retrieval and the integration of retrieved information. Its implementation involved extracting relevant features and ensuring seamless retrieval and integration.

V. DISCUSSION / A. Enhancements in Model Performance .. B. Implications for AI Application Development

RAG contributes access to broad knowledge bases and supports contextually rich and factually accurate outputs. Alternative retrieval and integration mechanisms are identified as a future research direction.

VI. CONCLUSION

RAG is integrated into the Mistral 8x7B LLM with MoE. Its integration is reported to improve information retrieval, reasoning, task performance, and the contextual richness, accuracy, and nuance of generated responses.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Achieving Higher Factual Accuracy in Llama LLM with Weighted Distribution of Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Zhenhua Gai · 2024-05-21

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a promising generation technique and retrieval-and-generative paradigm that augments language models with relevant information from external databases or a large corpus. Its central purpose is to ground outputs in factual data, improving factual accuracy, relevance, and contextual appropriateness while extending a model’s effective knowledge beyond its initial training data. It unfolds in two stages: first, a retrieval step uses the input query to select and rank relevant documents from a corpus through similarity scores; second, a generation step incorporates the selected documents, including through an attention mechanism, to guide output generation. Its effectiveness depends on the relevance and reliability of retrieved documents, efficient large-scale retrieval, and integrating that information without compromising fluency. In the described Llama integration, a weighted distribution prioritizes high-quality retrieved information during generation and is evaluated with precision, recall, F1 score, BLEU score, and human assessments. The records suggest that advanced retrieval algorithms and context-aware weighting could further improve robustness, adaptability, and multilingual applicability.

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Achieving Higher Factual Accuracy in Llama LLM with Weighted Distribution of Retrieval-Augmented Generation / Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is integrated with Llama through a weighted distribution mechanism. The resulting approach is evaluated using precision, recall, F1 score, BLEU score, and human assessments.

1. Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances language models by retrieving relevant information from external databases and incorporating it into the generation process. It is presented as a way to improve the relevance and factual accuracy of outputs while expanding the model’s effective knowledge base beyond its initial training data.

2. Literature Survey / 2.1. LLM Hallucination .. 2.3. LLM Benchmarks

Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines retrieval-based and generative approaches by incorporating relevant documents from a large corpus into the generation process. Its performance depends on the relevance and reliability of retrieved documents, the efficiency of large-scale retrieval, and the integration of retrieved information without compromising fluency.

3. Methodology / 3.1. Llama Large Language Model .. 3.4. Experimental Setup

Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines retrieval-based and generative models by selecting relevant documents from a corpus and using them to guide output generation. Its retrieval step ranks documents using similarity scores, and its generation step incorporates the selected documents through an attention mechanism. The unit states that RAG can improve the factual accuracy and contextual relevance of language model outputs.

5. Discussion

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is presented as a retrieval-and-generation approach whose weighted distribution can improve the factual grounding and contextual appropriateness of language-model outputs. The unit suggests that more advanced retrieval algorithms and context-aware weighting could further improve its robustness, adaptability, and multilingual applicability.

6. Conclusion

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is integrated into the Llama Large language model through a weighted distribution that prioritizes high-quality information during generation. Combining retrieval and generation is presented as a way to leverage their respective strengths.

retrieval augmented generation in Retrieval augmented text-to-SQL generation for epidemiological question answering using electronic health records

Angelo Ziletti · 2024-06-21

Retrieval augmented generation is a technology combined with text-to-SQL generation to answer epidemiological questions using electronic health records and claims data. It improves language-model and LLM performance for complex SQL generation by incorporating relevant dataset information. The approach masks entities to compute similarity and selects masked questions rather than queries, avoiding an initial SQL-generation call. It supplies relevant or random examples; relevant examples consistently improve accuracy, executability, and performance over static instruction prompting and advanced prompting, including all tested scenarios. More than one example often has diminishing returns. The work extends RAG evidence from general text-to-SQL benchmarks to small, domain-specific biomedical datasets.

Retrieval augmented generation is combined with text-to-SQL generation to answer epidemiological questions using electronic health records and claims data. It is presented as a promising direction for improving the capabilities of language models in a realistic industry setting.

1

3

4 / 4.1 .. 4.2

Retrieval augmented generation supplies relevant or random examples to the models. Relevant examples consistently improve performance over advanced prompting alone, while adding more than one example often provides diminishing returns.

5

RAG improved performance in all tested scenarios for answering epidemiological questions using real-world data. The work extends evidence for RAG's effectiveness from general text-to-SQL benchmarks to small, domain-specific biomedical datasets.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in FACTS About Building Retrieval Augmented Generation-based Chatbots

Rama Akkiraju, Anbang Xu, Deepak Bora, Tan Yu, Lu An, Vishal Seth, Aaditya Shukla, Pritam Gundecha, Hridhay Mehta, Ashwin Jha, Prithvi Raj, Abhinav Balasubramanian, Murali Maram, Guru Muthusamy, Shivakesh Reddy Annepally, Sidney Knowles, Min Du, Nick Burnett, Sean Javiya, Ashok Marannan, Mamta Kumari, Surbhi Jha, Ethan Dereszenski, Anupam Chakraborty, Subhash Ranjan, Amina Terfai, Anoop Surya, Tracey Mercer, Vinodh Kumar Thanigachalam, Tamar Bar, Sanjana Krishnan, Jasmine Jaksic, Nave Algarici, Jacob Liberman, Joey Conway, Sonu Nayyar and Justin Boitano · 2024-07-10

Retrieval Augmented Generation is a widely used RAG pipeline component and process in generative-AI-based chatbot construction. It combines retrieval with LLM generation: through semantic matching, it retrieves relevant, fresh enterprise information from vector databases and feeds it to large language models for response generation. Its design unfolds through document retrieval, query rephrasing, reranking, prompting, access controls, references, privacy safeguards, and agent orchestration. Its many control points require careful tuning. What matters most is quality across the FACTS dimensions: freshness, architecture, costs, testing and evaluation, and document security. Approaches discussed for improvement include domain-adapted models, HYDE, FLARE, Self-refine, ReAct, and automated evaluation with RAGAS and ARES.

ABSTRACT

Retrieval Augmented Generation is identified as a key technological component of generative-AI-based chatbots. The unit focuses on RAG-based chatbot design, including document retrieval, query rephrasing, reranking, prompting, access controls, references, privacy safeguards, and agent orchestration.

INTRODUCTION

Retrieval augmented generation is identified as a major development in chatbot construction. It combines retrieval with LLM generation so chatbots can access fresh enterprise content and synthesize responses.

CASE STUDY

RAGs are used with LLMs in the three bots built at NVIDIA.

ENSURING FRESHNESS OF ENTERPRISE .. 3.1

Retrieval Augmented Generation retrieves relevant information from vector databases through semantic matching and feeds it to LLMs for response generation. It enables vector databases and LLMs to work together to deliver up-to-date enterprise knowledge, but its many control points require careful tuning.

RELATED WORK

RAG is discussed as a system whose quality involves freshness, architecture, costs, testing, and security. The unit reviews approaches for improving RAG, including domain-adapted models, HYDE, FLARE, Self-refine, ReAct, and automated evaluation with RAGAS and ARES.

retrieval-augmented generation in RadioRAG: Online Retrieval-augmented Generation for Radiology Question Answering

Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh · 2024-07-22

Retrieval-augmented generation is a reasoning-engine approach in which language models use external sources to supply context, access up-to-date information, and mitigate outdated, inaccurate, or hallucinated responses through retrieved and cited material. It matters especially for knowledge-intensive and clinical settings, where it supports medical question answering, decision-making, and guideline interpretation. In RadioRAG, the approach unfolds from real-time retrieval of relevant Radiopaedia text fragments for an original radiology question to a final model that must give one concise answer based only on that context or say “I don't know.” This grounding generally improved factuality and accuracy, but irrelevant retrieved context and strict reliance on it could still produce hallucinations or incorrect diagnoses. Related work benchmarks and applies it across medicine, including radiology and hepatological guidelines.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

RadioRAG: Online Retrieval-augmented Generation for Radiology Question Answering

Retrieval-augmented generation appears in the title as the approach used for online radiology question answering.

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation is presented as a way to mitigate outdated or inaccurate model information by integrating outside data sources. Earlier systems used fixed, pre-assembled databases, whereas RadioRAG retrieves information in real time.

1. Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation is an approach in which large language models act as reasoning engines with access to external sources. It may reduce hallucinations through the use and citation of source material and provide access to up-to-date information beyond the model's training data.

2. Materials and Methods / 2.1. RSNA Cases .. 2.6. Code and Data Availability

Retrieval augmented generation was implemented in RadioRAG by supplying a final language model with the original radiology question and relevant text fragments retrieved from Radiopaedia. The model was instructed to answer in one concise sentence based solely on the provided context or to state “I don't know.”

4. Discussion

Retrieval-augmented generation was applied to radiological question answering through the RadioRAG framework. The approach generally improved factuality and accuracy by grounding responses in retrieved material, but strict reliance on irrelevant context could lead to hallucinations or incorrect diagnoses.

references

The references describe retrieval-augmented generation as a method for knowledge-intensive and clinical medical tasks. They examine its ability to reduce hallucination, support clinical medicine, benchmark medical question answering, optimize clinical decision-making, and improve interpretation of clinical guidelines.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in RAG-RLRC-LaySum at BioLaySumm: Integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Readability Control for Layman Summarization of Biomedical Texts

Yuelyu Ji, Zhuochun Li, Rui Meng, Sonish Sivarajkumar, Yanshan Wang, Zeshui Yu, Hui Ji, Yushui Han, Hanyu Zeng, Daqing He · 2024-08-16

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a solution for generating lay summaries by integrating trustworthy external knowledge. It processes entire papers despite limited input capacity, aiming for simplified, factually accurate, contextually relevant summaries with improved precision and pertinence. During inference, it uses an initial lay summary as a query, retrieves relevant Wikipedia descriptions through the Pyserini index, and reranks candidate passages with ColBERT or BGE-v2. It then generates a lay summary from the scientific document and retrieved grounding passages, using multiple knowledge sources.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is used to integrate trustworthy external knowledge into summary generation. In the proposed framework, it supports summaries that are intended to be simplified, factually accurate, and contextually relevant.

RAG processes entire papers despite limited input capacity and generates lay summaries using retrieved grounding passages. It uses an initial lay summary as a query during inference, retrieves relevant Wikipedia descriptions through a Pyserini index, and applies ColBERT or BGE-v2 as neural rerankers.

Retrieval-augmented Generation in SDG target detection in environmental reports using Retrieval-augmented Generation with LLMs

Darío Garigliotti · 2024-08-16

Retrieval-augmented Generation is a recently established framework that couples retrieval with Large Language Model-powered text generation to extend LLM capabilities with explicit contextual knowledge. It is useful in domain-specific scenarios and is used for question answering and for SDG target evidence identification and target detection in long, heterogeneous documents. Its three-part pipeline begins with retrieval: it selects and refines relevant passage candidates, indexing uniquely identified report passages for evidence identification and treating SDG targets as passages for target detection. Next, augmentation places the question and selected passages in a prompt. Finally, an LLM generates an answer from that context. Several methods are proposed and assessed within the framework; future work may complement retrieval with a claim detector.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

The Retrieval-augmented Generation (RAG) framework is used to address the manual inspection of long, heterogeneous documents. The paper proposes and evaluates methods within this framework for SDG target evidence identification and SDG target detection.

1

Retrieval-augmented Generation is described as a framework that begins by selecting passage candidates, applies a more advanced detection technique to refine relevance decisions, and couples this process with text generation powered by Large Language Models.

2

Retrieval-augmented Generation extends LLM capabilities by supplying additional explicit knowledge as context from which a generated answer can be produced. It is considered useful for domain-specific scenarios.

3 / 3.1 .. 3.3

Retrieval-augmented Generation is the framework used to approach both tasks. Its pipeline consists of retrieval, augmentation through a prompt containing the question and selected retrieved passages, and LLM-based answer generation.

4 / 4.1 .. 4.3

The RAG framework indexes uniquely identified report passages for the evidence identification task and treats SDG targets as passages for the target detection task.

6

Retrieval-augmented generation is the framework within which several methods are proposed and assessed. Future work may use a claim detector to complement its retrieval stage.

retrieval-augmented generation in Medical Graph RAG: Towards Safe Medical Large Language Model via Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Junde Wu, Jiayuan Zhu, Yunli Qi, Jingkun Chen, Min Xu, Filippo Menolascina, Vicente Grau · 2024-10-15

Retrieval-augmented generation is a non-finetuning retrieval technique that answers queries from specific, including private, datasets without additional model training. It improves response accuracy, reduces hallucinations, and has shown strong cited-response results, but can struggle to synthesize new insights or understand extensive documents holistically. In the case study, standard RAG is implemented with LangChain and compared under shared data with no retrieval, GraphRAG, and MedGraphRAG: it generally beats no retrieval but is surpassed by MedGraphRAG. Tier-by-tier additions yield limited gains. Medical use remains rarely explored and lacks needed evidence-based responses and term explanations.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation answers queries using specific and private datasets without additional model training. It can struggle to synthesize new insights and perform tasks requiring holistic understanding across extensive documents.

Experiment / Dataset / RAG data / Repository data / Test Data .. Case Study

Standard RAG is implemented with LangChain and is compared with no retrieval, GraphRAG, and MedGraphRAG under the same RAG and test data. It generally improves over no retrieval but is surpassed by MedGraphRAG in the reported evaluations.

Analysis / Ablation Study based on GraphRAG .. Which is important? Data or Method

RAG is compared with GraphRAG and MedGraphRAG for retrieving individual data tiers and incrementally accumulating all three tiers. With standard RAG, Med-Paper data improves performance by less than 2% and Med-Dictionary data by less than 1%, while adding all three tiers produces only mediocre improvements.

Related Work / LLM for Medicine .. Retrieval-augmented generation

Retrieval-augmented generation enables models to use specific datasets without additional training, improving response accuracy and reducing hallucinations. Its use in medical applications remains limited, and it lacks support for evidence-based responses and term explanations required in clinical settings.

retrieval-augmented generation in BlendFilter: Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Query Generation Blending and Knowledge Filtering

Haoyu Wang · 2024-11

Retrieval-augmented generation is a strategy for improving Large Language Model content by retrieving external knowledge documents and using them with a task input for generation. Its central challenge is that direct retrieval for complex questions can return unrelated documents that mislead the model, so retrieval alone does not reliably improve accuracy. It develops from early passive use of retrieved knowledge toward interactive retrieval, and is further enhanced by BlendFilter, which blends query generation, combines external and internal knowledge augmentation, and filters noisy knowledge.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

1

Retrieval-augmented generation integrates external knowledge sources, such as Wikipedia, to improve LLM-generated content. It typically sends a task input to a retriever and then uses the retrieved information with the input to generate content.

2

Retrieval-augmented generation improves Large Language Models by leveraging external knowledge. Early approaches treated the models as passive recipients, while later approaches enabled more interactive retrieval processes.

4 .. 4.8

The experiments assess BlendFilter as a method for enhancing retrieval-augmented generation. They show that retrieval alone does not consistently improve accuracy because unrelated retrieved documents can mislead the LLM, whereas BlendFilter combines queries and filters knowledge to improve generation.

5

Retrieval-augmented generation is enhanced by BlendFilter through the combination of external and internal knowledge augmentation, query generation blending, and filtering of retrieved knowledge. The approach is designed to address complex inputs and reduce noise.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation, abbreviated RAG, is a significant advancement and method in large language models. It integrates up-to-date information unavailable during initial training, broadening LLM applicability and practical utility in real-world applications. It can effectively mitigate hallucinations, but inaccurate outputs and persistent hallucination still limit continued use. Research focuses on enhancing LLM capabilities in RAG scenarios, while NewsBreak explores RAG systems to gather fragmented local data and organize it into coherent question-answering systems and informative resources.

RAG in Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs?

Zhuowan Li · 2024-11-12/2024-11-16

RAG, or retrieval-augmented generation, is a method and tool for large language models that retrieves information relevant to a query, then prompts a model to respond using the retrieved material as context. It augments models with information from various sources, supports language modeling and question answering, and expands access to large amounts of information at minimal cost. Conceptually, it acts as a prior and regularizes attention onto retrieved segments. Its central advantage is efficiency: by supplying selected segments rather than processing an entire long input, it uses fewer input tokens and has significantly lower computation cost than long-context LLMs. In the reported evaluation, contexts are divided into 300-word chunks and the top five chunks are selected by query-chunk cosine similarity using Contriever or Dragon. RAG is compared with long-context prompting on nine English, real, query-based datasets from LongBench and ∞Bench, with synthetic datasets also used as additional evaluation data. RAG generally has lower average performance than long-context processing when resources are sufficient, but its predictions overlap substantially: it makes identical predictions for 63% of queries, and 70% have an absolute prediction-score difference below 10. It can outperform long-context prompting for GPT-3.5-Turbo on En.QA and En.MC when text exceeds the model context window. Its errors can resemble long-context errors, while failures arise when retrieval must support multi-step reasoning or handle general, long, complex, or implicit queries. Retrieval quality may be improved through correction, critique, verification, and adaptive search. Overall, RAG remains a viable, lower-cost option for inputs far beyond a model’s context window and a target for further optimization.

Narrative, section by section

7 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval Augmented Generation is compared with long-context LLMs across public datasets. It has lower cost than long-context processing but lower average performance when resources are sufficient.

Introduction

Retrieval augmented generation is described as an effective and efficient approach for large language models to leverage external knowledge. It retrieves information relevant to a query and prompts an LLM to generate a response using that information as context.

opening

Retrieval-augmented generation reduces input length by supplying retrieved segments, making it significantly more cost-efficient than long-context processing. It generally underperforms long-context LLMs, although its predictions are identical to theirs for over 60% of queries.

Related Work

Retrieval-augmented generation augments LLMs with relevant information retrieved from various sources. It has been successful for language modeling and question answering, with significantly lower computation cost.

opening .. Benchmarking results

RAG is evaluated against long-context prompting on nine English, real, query-based datasets from LongBench and ∞Bench. Its retrieval setup divides contexts into 300-word chunks and selects the top five chunks by query-chunk cosine similarity, using either Contriever or Dragon.

opening .. Exclusion of LLM’s internal knowledge

RAG generally underperforms LC, although it can outperform LC for GPT-3.5-Turbo on the longer ∞Bench En.QA and En.MC datasets when the context exceeds the model’s context window. Its failures are associated with multi-step reasoning, general or complex queries, and implicit questions requiring broad context understanding. RAG uses fewer input tokens than LC and can answer a substantial portion of queries, motivating its use within SELF-ROUTE.

conclusion

RAG has lower computational cost than LC and remains viable when inputs considerably exceed the model’s context window size. It is also identified as a subject for future optimization.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in HyPA-RAG: A Hybrid Parameter Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for AI Legal and Policy Applications

Rishi Kalra, Zekun Wu, Ayesha Gulley, Airlie Hilliard, Xin Guan, Adriano Koshiyama, Philip Treleaven · 2024-11-16

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a system and proposed solution for Large Language Model limitations, including outdated knowledge and hallucinations. It enhances pre-trained sequence-to-sequence models by incorporating external knowledge through indexing, retrieval, and generation. Using sparse and dense retrieval, including BM25, vector retrieval, and neural embeddings, it aims to improve response specificity, accuracy, and grounding for varied, complex queries, including interpretation of AI legal texts. It is evaluated with retrieval, answer-quality, correctness, Faithfulness, and Correctness measures across chunking and parameter configurations. Adaptive configurations, query rewrites, and reranking generally outperform fixed-k and LLM-only systems, though performance involves trade-offs. Retrieval errors, poor context integration, and high costs remain challenges. Human feedback could support optimization, evaluation, and metric alignment, while transparency and reproducibility are emphasized through documented data, methods, and metrics.

Narrative, section by section

7 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation improves response accuracy by integrating external knowledge. In interpreting AI legal texts, it can struggle with retrieval errors, poor context integration, and high costs.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances Large Language Models by incorporating external knowledge. The unit proposes it as a response to outdated model knowledge and hallucinations, while noting that it introduces additional challenges.

Background and Related Work

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances pre-trained sequence-to-sequence models by integrating external knowledge through indexing, retrieval, and generation. It combines sparse and dense retrieval techniques, including BM25 and vector retrieval, to improve response specificity, accuracy, and grounding.

Performance Evaluation / Dataset Generation .. Classifier Results

The RAG system is evaluated with retrieval, answer-quality, and correctness metrics across chunking strategies and parameter configurations. Adaptive configurations generally outperform fixed-k and LLM-only systems on the reported Faithfulness and Correctness measures.

Overall Results and Discussion

The system benefits from adaptive parameters such as query rewrites and reranking. Its performance reflects trade-offs between faithfulness, answer quality, and correctness.

Limitations and Future Work

The RAG system is the subject of the optimisation feedback loop shown in Figure 4, where human feedback could support evaluation and metric alignment.

Ethical and Societal implications

The findings enhance understanding of RAG systems in legal contexts. The unit emphasizes transparency and reproducibility by documenting data generation, retrieval methods, and evaluation metrics.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Ask in Any Modality

Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Amirhosein Zobeiri, Mahdi Dehghani, Mohammadali Mohammadkhani, Bardia Mohammadi, Omid Ghahroodi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah, Ehsaneddin Asgari · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a retriever-generator pipeline that addresses language-model limitations by dynamically retrieving, selecting, and incorporating external knowledge. Embedding models and possible re-ranking identify relevant passages for generation, improving factual grounding, coherence, and knowledge-intensive tasks while reducing hallucinations and outdated knowledge. It advances through planning-guided retrieval, agentic RAG, and feedback-driven iterative refinement.

Narrative, section by section

front matter .. Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation mitigates hallucinations and outdated knowledge by integrating external dynamic information to improve the factual grounding of generated outputs.

Introduction & Background

Retrieval-Augmented Generation addresses limitations of language models by retrieving and incorporating external knowledge, improving factual accuracy and reducing hallucinations. Its retriever-generator pipeline uses embedding models and possible re-ranking to select relevant passages, which the generator then uses to produce more informed and coherent responses. Planning-guided retrieval, agentic RAG, and feedback-driven iterative refinement have further advanced its retrieval and generation components.

regular RAG in CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Nengbo Wang, Xiaotian Han, Jagdip Singh, Jing Ma, Vipin Chaudhary · 2025

Regular RAG is a standard baseline RAG variant that chunks external knowledge into minimal units and retrieves from a vector database through semantic search and query similarity. It is evaluated with context recall and context precision. It struggles with grounded context and identifying how retrieved content relates to the user query: chunking can break linguistic and logical connections, while semantic similarity can return superficially relevant but causally irrelevant material. In a case study, it retrieves relevant yet overly general passages and misses the concrete mechanism linking influence tactics to sales contract wins.

Narrative, section by section

3 sections; each heading opens the text

opening

Regular RAG struggles to retrieve truly grounded context and to accurately discern the relationship between retrieved content and the user query. CausalRAG is evaluated against regular RAG and is reported to achieve superior performance across different contexts.

Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs

Regular RAG commonly chunks documents into minimal units, which can disrupt natural linguistic and logical connections. Its semantic search can retrieve information that is superficially similar but causally irrelevant, and low retrieval precision can introduce bias that reduces generation accuracy.

Experiment / Experimental Setup .. Parameter Study

Regular RAG serves as a baseline that relies solely on semantic similarity for retrieval. In the case study, it retrieves relevant but overly general passages and fails to preserve the concrete mechanism connecting influence tactics to sales contract wins.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in CausalRAG: Integrating Causal Graphs into Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Nengbo Wang, Xiaotian Han, Jagdip Singh, Jing Ma, Vipin Chaudhary · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a framework and generation paradigm that combines retrieval mechanisms with generative capabilities. It enhances large language model performance on knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating external knowledge, improving contextual understanding and response quality. Its central challenges are that text chunking can disrupt contextual integrity, retrieval may favor semantic similarity over causal relevance, and document selection may be inaccurate, producing shallow responses without essential details. It is evaluated with context recall and context precision, while research advances retrieval efficiency, integration mechanisms, and the representation and use of external knowledge for deeper reasoning and generation, including knowledge graphs. The approach unfolds toward CausalRAG, which integrates causality into retrieval-augmented generation: it retrieves causally relevant evidence and combines the user query with a causal summary, addressing limitations of existing systems.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances large language model capabilities by integrating external knowledge. The abstract presents it as the broader approach that includes traditional RAG systems and the proposed CausalRAG framework.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation has emerged as a promising framework for addressing the limitations of large language models. It combines retrieval mechanisms with generative capabilities to enhance contextual understanding and response quality.

opening

RAG architectures are described as having three critical limitations: text chunking can disrupt contextual integrity, retrieval can rely on semantic similarity rather than causal relevance, and document selection can lack accuracy. These limitations can lead to seemingly relevant but shallow responses that lack essential details.

Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Rethinking Graph-based RAGs

Retrieval-augmented generation enhances large language models' ability to handle knowledge-intensive tasks by integrating external knowledge retrieval. Research on it focuses on improving retrieval and integration mechanisms, as well as representing and using external knowledge for deeper reasoning and generation.

Methodology .. Retrieving Context Causally

Retrieval-augmented generation is integrated with causality in CausalRAG to focus responses on causally relevant evidence rather than loosely related text. The resulting prompt combines the user query with a causal summary.

Conclusion and Future Work

CausalRAG is presented as a framework that integrates causal reasoning into retrieval-augmented generation to address limitations in existing systems.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in DioR: Adaptive Cognitive Detection and Contextual Retrieval Optimization for Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Hanghui Guo, Jia Zhu, Shimin Di, Weijie Shi, Zhangze Chen, Jiajie Xu · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates external knowledge bases and retrieves external data resources during generation, using language models' contextual learning to reduce erroneous information and improve reliability and precision. It enhances use of non-parametric knowledge and is studied for mitigating hallucination issues in large language models. Methods are compared on four datasets, with DioR reported higher-performing and proposed to improve retrieval-trigger control and scrutiny of retrieved content.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates external knowledge bases into the generation process and uses the contextual learning capabilities of language models to reduce erroneous information and improve reliability and precision.

Related Work

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances a model's ability to use non-parametric knowledge by retrieving external data resources.

Experiment / Experimental Setups .. Ablation Experiment

The unit compares DioR with various retrieval-augmented generation methods, including SEAKR, RaDIO, Dragin, wo-RAG, SR-RAG, FL-RAG, FS-RAG, and FLARE. DioR generally achieves higher reported performance on the four datasets.

Conclusion and Future work

The paper investigates the effectiveness of RAG techniques in mitigating hallucination issues in LLMs. It proposes DioR as an improved dynamic RAG approach that addresses retrieval-trigger control and scrutiny of retrieval content.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Zhitong Wang, Cheng Gao, Chaojun Xiao, Yufei Huang, Shuzheng Si, Kangyang Luo, Yuzhuo Bai, Wenhao Li, Tangjian Duan, Chuancheng Lv, Guoshan Lu, Gang Chen, Fanchao Qi, Maosong Sun · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a method and approach for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks that integrates large language models with external, large-scale textual knowledge. It aims to improve response quality and mitigate or reduce hallucinations, including through up-to-date information dynamically retrieved from Wikipedia in real time. It is widely applied to law, medicine, and finance. Its central challenge is document segmentation: effective chunking supports retrieval and generation, yet existing methods mostly focus on retrievers, the RAG pipeline, or generation reliability while overlooking chunk quality. In its evaluation setting, retrieved chunks are concatenated with input instructions before answer generation. The records conclude that document segmentation is critical but underexplored in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-augmented generation integrates external knowledge to enhance large language models. The unit presents PIC as a method intended to improve its document chunking component.

1 / Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates large language models with large-scale textual knowledge to improve response quality and mitigate hallucinations. The unit identifies document segmentation as an underexplored but important challenge in RAG systems.

2 / Related Works

Retrieval-Augmented Generation has been shown to be effective for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks. Existing methods mainly improve retriever performance, design the broader RAG pipeline, or enhance the reliability of language-model generation, but most overlook the impact of chunk quality on downstream performance.

3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions

Retrieval-augmented generation requires an effective chunking strategy to support retrieval and generation performance.

4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the application setting used to evaluate the chunking methods. Retrieved chunks are concatenated with input instructions before answer generation.

7 / Conclusions / Limitations

The paper identifies document segmentation as a critical yet underexplored challenge in retrieval-augmented generation systems.

Retrieval Augmented Generation in Fact, Fetch, and Reason: A Unified Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Satyapriya Krishna, Kalpesh Krishna, Anhad Mohananey, Steven Schwarcz, Adam Stambler, Shyam Upadhyay, Manaal Faruqui · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a system requiring Large Language Models to understand queries, retrieve relevant information, and synthesize accurate responses. It combines retrieval and generation for multi-hop reasoning, factual grounding, and information synthesis across diverse domains. FRAMES evaluates it end to end through factuality, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning to support more robust, efficient systems, while research raises concerns about source bias, misuse, and environmental impact.

Retrieval-augmented generation systems require Large Language Models to understand queries, retrieve relevant information, and synthesize accurate responses. FRAMES evaluates these capabilities together in end-to-end scenarios.

Retrieval-augmented generation combines the strengths of retrieval systems and the generative capabilities of Large Language Models. The unit presents FRAMES as an evaluation framework for assessing such systems in multi-hop, factually grounded, and multi-document settings.

2

Retrieval Augmented Generation is evaluated by FRAMES as an end-to-end system involving factuality, retrieval, and reasoning. FRAMES aims to support the development of more robust and efficient Retrieval Augmented Generation systems.

5

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is evaluated in FRAMES across factuality, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning.

Ethical Considerations

Retrieval-augmented generation research is associated with ethical considerations involving information-source biases, potential misuse of advanced systems, and environmental impact.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in HYBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases

Meng-Chieh Lee, Qi Zhu, Costas Mavromatis, Zhen Han, Soji Adeshina, Vassilis N. Ioannidis, Huzefa Rangwala, Christos Faloutsos · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a retrieval method and natural language processing technique for knowledge-intensive tasks. It retrieves textual documents to assist large language models in question answering, giving them access to unstructured document databases so they can address unknown facts and Open-Domain Question Answering. Its central limitation is that its text-focused retrieval overlooks interconnections among documents, so it does not meet relational hybrid questions. It is evaluated end to end on CRAG, where HYBGRAG reports higher combined scores than listed text-only, graph-only, text-and-graph, corrective, and self-reflective alternatives.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in HopRAG: Multi-Hop Reasoning for Logic-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Hao Liu, Zhengren Wang, Xi Chen, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Qinhan Yu, Wentao Zhang · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a generation system and standard approach for large language models on knowledge-intensive tasks. It addresses knowledge limitations by incorporating a retrieval module that fetches relevant information from external knowledge sources, using a passage corpus, query, and retrieved passage context to support response generation. It significantly improves large language models and enables easy interpretability and provenance tracking. Its effectiveness depends on relevant retrieval, but it often struggles with imperfect retrieval, which can produce inaccurate or incomplete responses when retrievers favor lexical or semantic similarity over logical relevance.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often struggle with imperfect retrieval when traditional retrievers prioritize lexical or semantic similarity over logical relevance. HopRAG is proposed as a framework to address this problem.

Retrieval-augmented generation has become a standard approach for large language models on knowledge-intensive tasks. Its effectiveness depends heavily on retrieving relevant documents, and imperfect retrieval can lead to inaccurate or incomplete responses.

2 / Related Work .. Tree&Graph-structured RAG

It improves large language models by incorporating a retrieval module that fetches relevant information from external knowledge sources. Its retrieval methods have evolved from sparse and dense retrievers to approaches that determine whether and when retrieval is needed.

3 / Method .. Algorithm

The retrieval-augmented generation system uses a passage corpus, a query, and a retrieved context of passages to support large language model response generation.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Investigating Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Quranic Studies: A Study of 13 Open-Source Large Language Models

Zahra Khalila, Arbi Haza Nasution, Winda Monika, Aytug Onan, Yohei Murakami, Yasir Bin Ismail Radi, Noor Mohammad Osmani · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a method that addresses problems associated with using separate models by gathering relevant knowledge before generating a response. It combines semantic retrieval with large language model generation, integrating large language model semantics and a vector database to search vectorized descriptive datasets. Relevant entries are supplied to models, enabling contextually relevant, dataset-based answers grounded in authoritative, contextually appropriate, external domain-specific knowledge and accompanied by citations for traceability and transparency. Its central effects are improved response quality and relevance, reduced hallucinations, and more reliable outputs. In the evaluated models, large models benefit most, while medium and small models improve but remain limited in integrating retrieved knowledge. It is also applied in the medical domain to mitigate retrieval and generation issues.

Narrative, section by section

5 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract—Accurate and contextually faithful responses are

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is used to address problems associated with using separate models. It enables the system to gather relevant knowledge before generating a response.

I.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates large language model semantics with a vector database to retrieve relevant information from descriptive datasets. In this study, it is used to reduce hallucination, improve response relevance, ground answers in authoritative and contextually appropriate sources, and provide citations that support traceability and transparency.

II.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines semantic retrieval with language-model generation in the study. It retrieves relevant entries from the vectorized dataset and supplies them to large language models so they can produce contextually relevant, dataset-based responses with citations.

IV.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation improves response quality by supplying models with external knowledge before they formulate responses. The framework benefits large models most strongly, while medium and small models also improve but remain limited in their ability to integrate retrieved knowledge.

V.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation improved response quality by grounding answers in external domain-specific knowledge, reducing hallucinations, and supporting more reliable outputs.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for LLM-based Recommendation

Shijie Wang, Wenqi Fan, Yue Feng, Shanru Lin, Xinyu Ma, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a method and generative-AI technology that leverages external knowledge sources or databases to supply an LLM with specific, relevant, and up-to-date knowledge. It retrieves fragments from a large corpus or external knowledge base to guide generation, combining retrieval systems with language models to produce coherent and informative text. This can enhance LLM understanding and generation, mitigate hallucinations and knowledge gaps, and enable effective recommendations without costly fine-tuning. However, vanilla or standard methods can introduce unnecessary noise, overlook structural relationships in knowledge, and fail to retrieve all relevant textual chunks because of harmful document disturbance.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Zirui Guo, Lianghao Xia, Yanhua Yu, Tu Ao, Chao Huang · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a system that enhances large language models by integrating external knowledge sources. It combines a user query with pertinent documents from an external knowledge database through essential retrieval and generation modules, formally represented as M(q; D) = G(q, ψ(q; ˆD)), with ˆD = φ(D). Retrieval improves inputs by finding relevant external information and grounds responses in factual, domain-specific knowledge, enabling more accurate, contextually relevant responses tailored to user needs. Existing approaches can use flat data representations, fragmented text chunks, and top-k contexts, producing inadequate contextual awareness and limited global coverage. Graph-based indexing and dual-level retrieval are presented to address these limitations and complex interdependencies.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems enhance large language models by integrating external knowledge sources to produce more accurate and contextually relevant responses. Existing systems can rely on flat data representations and insufficient contextual awareness, leading to fragmented answers that miss complex interdependencies.

Introduction

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates external knowledge sources with large language models to improve the accuracy and contextual relevance of generated responses. The unit presents graph-based indexing and dual-level retrieval as ways to address limitations in existing approaches.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Retrieval-Augmented Generation integrates user queries with pertinent documents from an external knowledge database through retrieval and generation components. Its framework is formally represented as M(q; D) = G(q, ψ(q; ˆD)), with ˆD = φ(D).

Related Work / Retrieval-Augmented Generation .. Large Language Model for Graphs

Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems enhance large language model inputs by retrieving relevant information from external sources and grounding responses in factual, domain-specific knowledge. Many current approaches embed queries in a vector space and retrieve the nearest context vectors, but their reliance on fragmented text chunks and top-k contexts can limit coverage of global information.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Chia-Yuan Chang, Zhimeng Jiang, Vineeth Rakesh, Menghai Pan, Chin-Chia Michael Yeh, Guanchu Wang, Mingzhi Hu, Zhichao Xu, Yan Zheng, Mahashweta Das, Na Zou · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is an approach and RAG solution for limitations of Large Language Models, addressing outdated or incorrect information by integrating real-time document retrieval and external knowledge to ground LLM outputs. Its main challenge is that retrieved documents may be irrelevant, noisy, or poorly ordered, with models emphasizing the beginning and end of long contexts. Standard baselines prepend retrieved documents to a query before a pre-trained LLM; MAIN-RAG improves these training-free baselines by filtering noisy candidates and ranking the remaining documents.

Narrative, section by section

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation incorporates external, real-time information retrieval to ground Large Language Model responses. Its existing systems can struggle with the quality of retrieved documents.

1 / Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation integrates real-time document retrieval to ground LLM outputs in external knowledge. Its effectiveness can be reduced when retrieved documents are irrelevant or noisy.

3 / Multi-Agent Filtering RAG (MAIN-RAG) .. 3.3 / Adaptive Judge Bar τq

The unit examines how document ordering affects prediction performance in retrieval-augmented generation. It motivates filtering and sorting documents because language models may emphasize information at the beginning and end of long contexts.

4 / Experiments .. 4.6 / Case Studies of Different Adaptive Judge

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is represented by baselines that prepend retrieved documents to a query before passing it to a pre-trained LLM, as well as by trained retrieval models. The experiments show that MAIN-RAG improves over standard training-free retrieval baselines by filtering noisy candidate documents and ranking the remaining ones.

retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Chia-Yuan Chang, Zhimeng Jiang, Vineeth Rakesh, Menghai Pan, Chin-Chia Michael Yeh, Guanchu Wang, Mingzhi Hu, Zhichao Xu, Yan Zheng, Mahashweta Das, Na Zou · 2025

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a system that retrieves documents for each query and uses them during language-model inference. It often struggles with insufficient-quality, irrelevant, or noisy retrievals, which can mislead models, degrade performance, raise computational overhead, and undermine reliability. Its central challenge is noise robustness. RAG includes training-based and training-free methods; the unit focuses on filtering noisy documents after retrieval to improve accuracy, reliability, and robustness, ending with MAIN-RAG addressing these retrieval challenges.

Retrieval-augmented generation, referred to as RAG in the unit, is the setting in which MAIN-RAG addresses noisy document retrieval challenges.

retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in Mitigating the Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via Pure Synthetic Data

Shenglai Zeng, Jiankun Zhang, Pengfei He, Jie Ren, Tianqi Zheng, Hanqing Lu, Han Xu, Hui Liu, Yue Xing, Jiliang Tang · 2025

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a generation system and language-modeling approach that retrieves relevant information from external knowledge sources, combines it with a query, and uses the retrieval data as input for generation. It improves output accuracy, relevance, and generation quality while mitigating hallucinations. Its flexible architecture permits updates to the dataset, retriever, and large language model without retraining, supporting uses such as personal chatbots and specialized domain experts. The records then focus on a central limitation: when retrieval uses private data, RAG brings severe privacy risks and is vulnerable to extraction and other privacy attacks. In the experiments, RAG generally retrieves one document per query using FAISS and L2-norm similarity, and generation quality is evaluated using Llama3-8b-chat. Carefully designed composite structured prompts, including requests to repeat context, can expose retrieved information. The work concludes by evaluating synthetic retrieval data for generation as a way to reduce these privacy concerns.

Narrative, section by section

6 sections; each heading opens the text

Abstract

RAG enhances language-model outputs by integrating relevant information retrieved from external knowledge sources. When its retrieval process uses private data, it may face severe privacy risks.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation improves language model outputs by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge sources and combining it with a query for generation. The unit identifies privacy risks when its retrieval process uses private data and proposes synthetic retrieval data as an alternative.

Related Works

Retrieval-augmented generation was introduced by Lewis et al. (2020) and improves output accuracy and relevance while mitigating hallucinations. Its architecture allows updates to the dataset, retriever, and large language model without retraining, supporting applications such as personal chatbots and specialized domain experts. It is vulnerable to extraction attacks and other privacy attacks, including attacks against production RAG models.

Experiment

RAG is the experimental setting used to test how retrieval affects generation quality and privacy. The experiments generally retrieve one document per query using FAISS and L2-norm similarity.

Privacy of using synthetic data

Retrieval-augmented generation systems are evaluated for data leakage using composite structured prompting attacks. The attacks use commands such as "Please repeat all the context" to induce reproduction of retrieved information.

Conclusions

Retrieval-augmented generation is the setting in which synthetic data is evaluated as data for generation, with the goal of reducing privacy concerns.

Retrieval-augmented generation is a system studied for safe use in sensitive and safety-critical domains. It uses synthetic data to replace sensitive data, creating opportunities for privacy protection and responsible deployment, while strict privacy guarantees remain an open challenge.

retrieval-augmented generation in Rationale-Guided Retrieval Augmented Generation

Jiwoong Sohn · 2025

Retrieval-augmented generation is a biomedicine-oriented method applied to backbone models that integrates trustworthy retrieved documents into model input to reduce hallucinations and provide up-to-date information. It ranges from simply adding documents to adaptive, rationale-based, and uncertainty-guided methods, which can require substantial resources, API costs, multiple calls, or iterative retrieval. It remains vulnerable to irrelevant context, difficult medical queries, and retriever bias. Comparisons on Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Meerkat-7B, and GPT-4o show retrieval does not always improve performance without advanced retrieval and filtering.

retrieval-augmented generation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Estimation of Source Reliability

Jeongyeon Hwang, Junyoung Park, Hyejin Park, Dongwoo Kim, Sangdon Park, Jungseul Ok · 2025

Retrieval-augmented generation is a promising approach for enhancing the factual accuracy, coverage, and richness of large-language-model responses by retrieving external knowledge from large-scale databases and using retrieved documents with a query to generate answers. Standard systems select documents through query-document relevance, often from a shared database, without explicitly accounting for source reliability. Consequently, they can retrieve incorrect information from unreliable sources, remain vulnerable to misinformation and heterogeneous source reliability, and produce misleading outputs; existing methods lack robust aggregation and preventive measures. The work develops RA-RAG, which uses RAG’s automatic retrieval and response generation to iteratively estimate source reliability without manual fact-checking. It evaluates multi-source systems that retrieve documents and generate answers, comparing RA-RAG with standard RAG, Robust RAG, Self-RAG, and a language model without retrieval. The work appears in the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing proceedings, pages 34279–34303.

Narrative, section by section

7 sections; each heading opens the text

front matter .. Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Estimation of Source Reliability / Abstract

Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances the factual accuracy of large language models by retrieving information from external databases. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation can retrieve incorrect information because it relies solely on query-document relevance and overlooks differences in source reliability.

Introduction

Retrieval-augmented generation leverages external knowledge from large-scale databases to improve coverage and generate richer responses. However, it can retrieve incorrect information from unreliable sources.

Related Works

Retrieval-augmented generation systems use retrieved information from external sources, but existing retrieval improvements remain vulnerable to misinformation because they rely on relevance measures between queries and documents. The unit argues that RAG systems need robust aggregation mechanisms for sources with varying reliability.

Problem Formulation / Standard RAG .. Multi-source RAG with source reliability

Retrieval-augmented generation uses retrieved documents together with a query to support language-model response generation. In the standard framework, the retrieved documents come from a shared database without explicitly accounting for source reliability.

Method: RA-RAG .. Iterative reliability estimation

RAG provides the ability to retrieve relevant documents and generate responses automatically, which enables RA-RAG to estimate reliability without manual fact-checking.

Experiments / Experimental setups .. Ablation studies and analysis

Retrieval-augmented generation is evaluated through multi-source systems that retrieve documents and generate answers from them. The experiments compare RA-RAG with standard RAG, Robust RAG, Self-RAG, and a language model without retrieval.

Conclusion

RAG systems are vulnerable to heterogeneous source reliability because they lack preventive measures against retrieving incorrect documents from unreliable sources, which can lead to misleading outputs.

standard RAG framework in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Estimation of Source Reliability

Standard RAG is a retrieval-augmented generation framework with database D, retriever R, and large language model G. Given a query, it retrieves the top-K documents by query-document relevance and uses them with the query to generate a response. Its key limitation is overlooking heterogeneous source reliability, allowing unreliable documents to influence answers.

Narrative, section by section

2 sections; each heading opens the text

Introduction

Standard RAG retrieves documents based on query-document relevance without distinguishing between sources. This can allow incorrect information from unreliable sources to influence the generated answer.

Problem Formulation / Standard RAG .. Multi-source RAG with source reliability

The standard RAG framework consists of a database D, a retriever R, and a large language model G. Given a query, it retrieves the top-K most relevant documents and uses them with the query to generate a response, but it overlooks heterogeneity in source reliability.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation in SEAKR: Self-aware Knowledge Retrieval for Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation

Zijun Yao · 2025

Retrieval-Augmented Generation is typically a system and strategy for combating hallucination in large language models. It retrieves external knowledge and integrates it into an LLM’s context to support question answering, aiming to increase factual correctness and trustworthiness. It combines a search engine with a Large Language Model: given a question, the search engine finds relevant knowledge snippets, then the model uses machine reading comprehension to generate an answer. Its methods include non-adaptive and adaptive approaches used for comparison on question answering tasks.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation retrieves and integrates external knowledge into the context of large language models. It is presented as a strategy for combating hallucination.

Retrieval-augmented generation methods are used as the main comparison class for SEAKR on question answering tasks. The comparison includes non-adaptive methods such as IRCoT and adaptive methods such as Self-RAG, FLARE, and DRAGIN.

Ethical Considerations

Retrieval augmented generation is described as an approach intended to increase the factual correctness of LLMs and improve their trustworthiness.
